**Given** the KTDA ERP adapter or the ERP itself is registered as an API client with scopes orders.read and products.write (ERP not named, KG-03), **when** it reads paid orders and writes product data, **then** both calls succeed through the same endpoints and rules as any other client.

**Given** a bank system is registered as an API client with scope payments.notify (bank not named, KG-04), **when** it posts a payment notification carrying a payment reference and an amount, **then** the notification is passed to PAY matching (PAY-005, BR-PAY-021); the API never marks an order paid itself; the response returns the matching result.

**Given** a shipping system is registered as an API client with scope shipments.write, **when** it posts a tracking event for a shipment, **then** the event is submitted to the tracking event hub through IC-TRK-01 (SubmitEvents); TRK-002 owns the code mapping; shipment status changes only through IOrderProcessingService.ShipAsync / DeliverAsync called by the hub.

**Given** an API client holds scope documents.read, **when** it requests the documents of an order it may see, **then** it receives document metadata and download links; document content is owned by the DOC module.

**Given** a new external system is registered with only the scopes it needs, **when** it calls an endpoint outside those scopes, **then** the API returns 403 and records the refusal (AUD-INT-007); calls inside its scopes succeed.

**Given** an authorization server is configured for the API (gateway product or custom build: decision API-GW; Web API base: decision API-01), **when** a partner system requests a token with the OAuth 2.0 client-credentials grant, **then** it receives a token carrying only its granted scopes, and calls made with that token succeed within those scopes.
basis: REQ-MPC-FR-338; FIT (: the licensed Web API plugin uses JWT; OAuth 2.0 / OIDC needs a gateway or custom build)

criterion: **Given** a call carries no token, an expired token or a token with a bad signature, **when** it reaches the API, **then** the API returns 401 and no data is read or changed.

**Given** a partner user signs in to a partner application through OpenID Connect, **when** the application calls the API with that user's token, **then** the user is mapped to one customer account (by the subject identifier stored on the account) and only that account's data is returned; an unmapped user gets 403.

**Given** a rate limit is set for an API client (value not stated), **when** the client exceeds it within the window, **then** further requests in that window get 429 and are not processed; other clients are not affected (BR-INT-004).

**Given** only the native global limiter is configured (CommonConfig.PermitLimit in appsettings), **when** any caller exceeds it, **then** requests are rejected with CommonConfig.RejectionStatusCode (default 503); this limiter is per user name or host, not per API client, so per-client limits are enforced at the gateway (INT-002) or in the INT plugin.

**Given** version v1 is live and v2 is released, **when** a client keeps calling v1, **then** v1 keeps answering for the deprecation window (setting, default not stated); every v1 response carries a deprecation notice with the retirement date (BR-INT-003).

**Given** a change removes or renames a field, changes a type or changes the meaning of a value, **when** it is released, **then** it is released only in a new major version; the same version never changes incompatibly (BR-INT-003).
**Given** a version is released or deprecated, **when** the developer opens the change log, **then** the change log lists every added, changed and deprecated item of that version with its date.
**Given** the retirement date of v1 has passed, **when** a client calls v1, **then** the API returns 410 and no data is read or changed.

**Given** a mobile app client is registered with the customer-facing scopes, **when** a signed-in customer browses, fills a cart and places an order through the API, **then** prices, discounts, tax and the order created are the same as for the same customer on the web storefront, because the API uses the same native services; whether native apps are a deliverable is decision M-19.

**Given** a government or Malawi Post system is registered as an RPT-004 ExternalConsumer with its AuthorisedDatasets and is linked to an INT-001 API client, **when** that system requests a report dataset through the API, or the RPT-004 batch-file delivery runs (IC-RPT-04), **then** it receives only the datasets authorised in its ExternalConsumer record; a request for any other dataset gets 403 (AUD-INT-007); each delivery is logged by RPT (AUD-RPT-008), and batch files pass through the INT-004 message log with its retry.

**Given** GraphQL is enabled (option), **when** a client queries an order with selected fields of its items, **then** only the requested fields are returned, under the same scopes, store limits and rate limits as the REST API.

**Given** the INT scope catalogue lists products.read, products.read.unpublished, products.write, orders.read, search.read, payments.notify, shipments.write, documents.read and webhooks.manage (BR-INT-006), **when** an administrator assigns scopes to an API client, **then** only catalogue scopes can be assigned; a client holding only products.read can list products through the catalogue API (IC-CAT-01) and gets 403 when it creates or changes a product.

**Given** the gateway is deployed in front of the shop, **when** an external system calls a shop API, **then** the call reaches nopCommerce only through the gateway; a direct call to the API path from outside the gateway network is refused (network rule).

**Given** an INT adapter calls an external system and a gateway egress route is configured for that system, **when** the adapter sends a request, **then** the request passes through the gateway and appears in its traffic log.
**Given** a new external system is to connect, **when** it is registered in the gateway and given an API client (INT-001), **then** it can call only the routes assigned to it.

**Given** an administrator opens the integration console, **when** the console loads, **then** each endpoint is listed with its route, its credential status and its health status (up or down, last error time).

**Given** an administrator saves a credential in the console, **when** the credential is shown again, **then** it is masked; it is held in the gateway secret store and never written to a configuration pack (CFG-01).
**Given** a client application is not on the allowed list, **when** it calls an API, **then** the gateway rejects the call before it reaches nopCommerce.

**Given** a per-client rate limit and a throttling rule are set (values not stated), **when** the client exceeds the limit, **then** the gateway rejects or delays further calls in that window as the rule states.

**Given** an abuse-detection rule is set (for example repeated authentication failures from one client; threshold not stated), **when** the rule fires, **then** the client is blocked for the configured period and an alert is sent to the configured recipients.

**Given** the developer portal is published, **when** a partner developer opens it, **then** the reference for each published API version is shown, generated from that version's OpenAPI definition, and the developer can request credentials, which an administrator approves.

**Given** a connected system is registered, **when** an administrator views the registry, **then** the entry shows system name, owner, interface version, test endpoint and production endpoint; a change of version or endpoint is kept as history.

**Given** a CSV-to-JSON mapping is defined for a partner route, **when** the partner posts a CSV file, **then** the API receives the mapped JSON; a row that cannot be mapped is returned to the partner with the failing field.
**Given** an XML mapping is defined for a partner route, **when** the partner posts XML, **then** the API receives the mapped JSON and the response is converted back to XML.
**Given** the sandbox is set up with test data, **when** a partner calls the sandbox endpoint, **then** the call is answered by the test instance; no production data is read or changed.

**Given** the gateway validates tokens issued under OAuth 2.0 or OpenID Connect (issuer: decision API-GW), **when** a call carries an invalid or expired token, **then** the gateway rejects it before it reaches nopCommerce.

**Given** a subscription to order.placed is Active, **when** an order is placed (native OrderPlacedEvent), **then** the INT consumer only writes an IntegrationMessage (BR-INT-010); the delivery task posts it to the subscriber URL and records the result.

**Given** subscriptions to shipment.sent and shipment.delivered are Active, **when** IOrderProcessingService.ShipAsync or DeliverAsync runs (native ShipmentSentEvent, ShipmentDeliveredEvent), **then** one message per event is delivered to each subscriber.

**Given** a subscription to shipment.created is Active, **when** a shipment is created by any path (admin, API, adapter), **then** one message is delivered; it is raised from EntityInsertedEvent<Shipment>, because the native ShipmentCreatedEvent is published only by the admin AddShipment action.
basis: REQ-MPC-FR-166; FIT (Admin OrderController publishes ShipmentCreatedEvent; ShipmentService.InsertShipmentAsync publishes the entity event)

criterion: **Given** feature PRD-INT-003 is off for store S (setting productfeature.PRD-INT-003 read through IC-PLT-02, store value else shared value), **when** an order of store S is placed, **then** the INT consumer writes no IntegrationMessage for it and the delivery task sends nothing for store S (BR-INT-005).

**Given** an API client holds scope webhooks.manage, **when** it posts a subscription with an https URL and a list of event types, **then** the subscription is created as PendingVerification and becomes Active only after the URL answers the verification request (SM-INT-02).

**Given** a seller has an Active subscription, **when** an order with items of that seller and of another seller changes, **then** the seller receives the event with only that seller's order lines; events of orders without that seller's items are not sent (BR-INT-011).
**Given** a subscription URL is not https, **when** it is saved, **then** it is refused with message Int.WebhookUrlNotHttps (BR-INT-012).
**Given** a subscription to order.paid is Active, **when** an order is marked paid (native OrderPaidEvent), **then** one order.paid message is delivered.
**Given** a subscription to shipment.dispatched is Active, **when** a shipment is shipped (native ShipmentSentEvent), **then** one shipment.dispatched message is delivered.

**Given** EGV-002 raises the module event ServiceRequest.Submitted (application, service, agency, citizen, time) once when a ServiceApplication is created (AC-EGV-002-01-02), **when** that event is published, **then** the INT consumer writes one IntegrationMessage and one service_request.submitted message carrying those fields is delivered to each Active subscriber — held by FG-06 (EGV-002 is held).

**Given** a message is delivered, **when** the subscriber receives it, **then** the request carries the message id, the event type, a timestamp and a signature computed over the body with the subscription secret; the subscriber can verify it (BR-INT-012).

**Given** the subscriber answers with an error or does not answer within the timeout (setting, default not stated), **when** delivery is attempted, **then** the message is retried under the INT-004 policy with the same message id, so the subscriber can drop duplicates (BR-INT-013).

**Given** retries are exhausted, **when** the last attempt fails, **then** the message becomes DeadLettered (SM-INT-01), the subscription owner and administrators are notified, and the message can be replayed (INT-004).

**Given** a message is built, **when** its payload is created, **then** it carries entity type, entity id, status, time and a link to the INT-001 resource; personal data beyond identifiers is not included (data minimisation, SEC-012).

**Given** a latency threshold is set for an API or adapter (value not stated), **when** its measured response time stays above the threshold for the configured period, **then** an alert is sent to the configured recipients with the integration name and the measured value.
**Given** an error-rate threshold is set (value not stated), **when** failures exceed it in the configured period, **then** an alert is sent to the configured recipients.
**Given** integrations are running, **when** an administrator opens the health view, **then** each integration shows success count, failure count, latency and throughput for the selected period.

**Given** an adapter has had no successful exchange within its expected interval (setting, default not stated), **when** the health check runs, **then** the adapter is shown as down and an alert is sent.

**Given** an outbound message fails with a transient error (timeout, 5xx, connection refused), **when** the retry policy applies, **then** it is retried after the configured delays up to the configured number of attempts (settings, defaults not stated).
**Given** an outbound message fails with a permanent error (the receiver rejects the content), **when** the response is received, **then** it becomes DeadLettered at once without further retries.

**Given** the last retry fails, **when** the attempt is recorded, **then** the message becomes DeadLettered, appears in the dead-letter list with every attempt and error, and administrators are notified.

**Given** a user with Integrations.Core.Messages.Replay opens a dead-lettered message, **when** they replay or discard it, **then** a reason is mandatory (message Int.ReasonRequired if empty); replay re-queues the same message id; the action is audited (AUD-INT-003).

**Given** another module sends to an external system through IC-INT-09 Enqueue (channel, event type, entity, payload, correlation id), **when** the delivery fails, **then** the message follows the same retry, dead-letter, replay and alert rules as INT messages and appears in the same dead-letter list (one outbox, BR-INT-015).

**Given** an ERP adapter is active and posting is enabled for sales, **when** an order is paid (OrderPaidEvent), **then** the consumer only enqueues a posting; the posting task sends the sales document with order number, lines, tax and totals; the ERP reference is stored and the posting is Posted.
**Given** posting is enabled for refunds, **when** a refund is recorded (OrderRefundedEvent), **then** a refund or credit posting referencing the original posting is sent.

**Given** the adapter is set to summarised posting, **when** the posting period closes (period a setting, default not stated), **then** one summarised posting per period and posting type is sent instead of one per order.
**Given** the ERP rejects a posting, **when** the response is received, **then** the posting becomes Failed with the ERP reason, appears in the posting exceptions list and the order is not changed.

**Given** the master of record for products is the ERP (BR-INT-020), **when** the ERP sends a changed product, **then** the change is applied through IProductService; the SEC-004 audit trail records before and after.

**Given** the master of record for products is the ERP, **when** an administrator opens the product edit page, **then** fields managed by the ERP show message Int.ErpManagedField; a value changed there is not sent to the ERP and is replaced at the next synchronisation.

**Given** the master of record for customers is nopCommerce, **when** a customer is created or changed, **then** the consumer of EntityInsertedEvent<Customer> / EntityUpdatedEvent<Customer> enqueues the change and the adapter sends it to the ERP.
**Given** stock levels come from the ERP, **when** the ERP sends stock, **then** stock synchronisation is done by INV-012 on this framework, not by INT-005.

**Given** a developer starts a new ERP adapter, **when** they use the connector kit, **then** the kit gives a template adapter implementing IC-INT-03 and a contract test suite; the adapter is accepted only when every contract test passes against the ERP test system.

**Given** KTDA has named its ERP and its interface (KG-03) and the KTDA adapter is built on this framework, **when** a KTDA order is paid and a product changes in the ERP, **then** criteria AC-INT-005-01-01 and AC-INT-005-02-01 hold for that ERP — held by KG-03.

**Given** INT has registered the adapter operations a workflow step may call (operations of IC-INT-03, IC-INT-05 and IC-INT-06 that the active adapters support) in the ADM-002 step-operation catalogue through IC-ADM-01 RegisterStepOperation at installation, **when** an ADM-002 call-to-another-system step names such an operation and runs, **then** INT runs the operation on the adapter with the step payload and the correlation id, logs the call in the IntegrationMessage log (SM-INT-01) and returns the result or the error to the step; the timeout and retry count are those of the ADM step, not the INT-004 policy (BR-INT-023).

**Given** the adapter of a registered operation is not active, **when** a step names that operation and runs, **then** INT returns the error AdapterInactive and sends nothing; the step fails as ADM-002 defines (case Failed, ADM-009 exception).

**Given** the SAGE 200 adapter is configured with the posting specification Malawi Post provides, **when** the posting period closes, **then** one summarised posting per period and per posting type defined in that specification is sent to SAGE 200 and the SAGE reference stored — held by MG-09 (specification not received).

**Given** SAGE 200 rejects or does not acknowledge a posting, **when** the response or timeout is recorded, **then** the batch becomes Failed (SM-INT-03), finance staff are notified, and the batch is retried under the INT-004 policy; the period is not shown as posted.

**Given** a batch is Posted, **when** reconciliation runs, **then** platform totals per period and posting type are compared with the totals read back from SAGE 200 (or imported from a SAGE 200 file); each difference is listed as an exception.

**Given** an exception is listed, **when** a user with Integrations.Core.Posting.CreateEditDelete resolves it, **then** a note is mandatory and the resolution is audited (AUD-INT-005); when no exception is open the batch becomes Reconciled.

**Given** the PostGlobal interface specification is agreed and the adapter is configured, **when** an order to be handled by the postal network reaches the hand-off point (trigger to be fixed with the specification), **then** the order and shipment data are sent as the specification states and the PostGlobal reference is stored — held by FG-06 and the specification (not received).

**Given** PostGlobal returns an item or tracking identifier for a shipment, **when** the adapter receives it, **then** it is set on the shipment through IShipmentService.UpdateShipmentAsync (Shipment.TrackingNumber); native ShipmentTrackingNumberSetEvent is not raised by this path (it is raised only by the admin controller).

**Given** PostGlobal is registered as a subscriber of order and shipment events (INT-003), or the specification requires a push by the adapter, **when** an order is placed or paid, or a shipment is created, shipped or delivered, **then** PostGlobal is notified once per event through the INT-003 delivery with the INT-004 retry policy.

**Given** PostGlobal is registered as a TRK-002 tracking source (TrackingSource type PostGlobal) and its codes are mapped to the common event list in the TRK-002 source mapping table (SourceCodeMapping), **when** PostGlobal reports an event with a mapped code, **then** the INT-007 adapter submits it to TRK-002 through IC-TRK-01 with source code, reference, time and location; TRK-002 applies it with the mapped common code (BR-TRK-010); INT keeps no status map of its own (BR-INT-030).

**Given** PostGlobal reports an event whose code has no mapping in SourceCodeMapping, **when** the adapter submits it through IC-TRK-01, **then** TRK-002 marks it Rejected in its rejected-events queue (SM-TRK-01) and no customer notification is sent for it; after the mapping is added TRK staff reprocess it.

**Given** PostGlobal events exist for a shipment, **when** the customer or a stakeholder opens tracking (TRK-001, CRM-003), **then** the PostGlobal events applied by TRK-002 appear in the shipment timeline with common status, time and location.

**Given** a bank adapter implements the PAY-024 operations InitiatePayment, GetStatement and Payout that the bank supports (IC-PAY-01), **when** the statement task runs, **then** the statement lines are retrieved and handed to PAY-014 reconciliation.

**Given** the bank adapter offers account verification (IC-INT-04 VerifyAccount) and SEL-005 uses a bank check as its configured verification method for a seller bank payout account, **when** that account is PendingVerification (SM-SEL-04) and SEL-005 calls VerifyAccount, **then** INT-008 returns Match or Mismatch with the bank reference; SEL-005 sets the account Verified or Failed (INT-008 changes no account state itself); payouts are SEL-017.
**Given** the bank does not offer account verification, **when** SEL-005 calls VerifyAccount, **then** the adapter returns NotSupported and SEL-005 falls back to its other verification methods.

**Given** KTDA has named its bank and the bank interface (KG-04), **when** the KTDA bank adapter is configured, **then** statements and payment notifications from that bank reach PAY-005 and PAY-014 — held by KG-04.

**Given** a regulator connector and a submission type (report or complaint escalation) are configured, **when** a submission is prepared, **then** it is stored as PendingApproval (SM-INT-04) and nothing is sent; the preparer sees message Int.SubmissionAwaitingApproval.

**Given** a submission is PendingApproval, **when** a second user with Integrations.Core.GovSubmissions.Approve approves it, **then** it is sent through the connector and the response is stored; the approval is audited (AUD-INT-006).
**Given** the preparer tries to approve the own submission, **when** the approval is posted, **then** it is refused with message Int.CannotApproveOwn (BR-INT-040).
**Given** an approver declines a submission, **when** the decline is saved, **then** it is not sent and the reason is recorded.

**Given** a new government-system adapter implements IC-INT-05 and is installed as a plugin, **when** an administrator configures it, **then** it appears in the connector list and uses the same approval, retry and audit as other government connectors, with no change to the framework.

**Given** an outlet source system and its mapping are configured, **when** the outlet sync task runs, **then** each outlet is created or updated as a StorePickupPoint (bundled Pickup.PickupInStore) through IStorePickupPointService, linked to its external key; an outlet removed at the source is not deleted but closed through the LOG-003 outlet extension.
**Given** a service-catalogue source is configured, **when** the sync task runs, **then** service products are created or updated through IProductService by external key (CAT-026 service listings).

**Given** a tariff source is configured, **when** the sync task runs, **then** tariff rows are written to the LOG-002 fee tables with their effective dates; orders already placed keep the tariff in force when placed.

**Given** a record from the source fails validation, **when** the sync task runs, **then** that record is not applied, the others are, and the rejected record is reported with its reason in the message log (INT-004).

**Given** the master of record for an entity type is the platform (BR-INT-020), **when** an administrator changes such a record, **then** the change is sent to the MPC system; the sync task does not overwrite it.
basis: REQ-MPC-FR-349 ("between Platform and other MPC systems")

criterion: **Given** a sync connection is configured, **when** data is exchanged, **then** the transfer uses TLS and the credentials stored encrypted for that system; a call with invalid credentials is rejected and logged.

**Given** a plugin is built for nopCommerce 5.00 (target framework net10.0; plugin.json SupportedVersions contains 5.00), **when** it is uploaded and installed under Configuration > Local plugins by a user with Configuration.ManagePlugins and the application restarts, **then** its functions are available and no nopCommerce core file has changed.
basis: D; REQ-KTDA-NFR-001; FIT (5.00.1: BasePlugin, Admin PluginController; Libraries/Nop.Core/NopVersion.cs:11; Directory.Build.props:3)

criterion: **Given** a plugin's SupportedVersions does not contain 5.00 (for example a 4.90 build), **when** the application loads plugins, **then** the plugin is not loaded and is reported as incompatible with the current version.

**Given** a new module needs storefront output, reactions to events, background jobs or a replaced service, **when** it is built, **then** it uses widget zones (IWidgetPlugin), event consumers (IConsumer<T>), scheduled tasks (IScheduleTask) or a DI registration in INopStartup with Order of at least 3000 recorded in the DI-override register (L1 §6.2 principle 7).

**Given** a plugin is limited to store S and customer role R in its plugin.json (LimitedToStores, LimitedToCustomerRoles), **when** a customer of another store, or without role R, uses the shop, **then** the plugin is not active for them.

**Given** an INT plugin is installed and its key catalogue lists every INT setting key with type, layer, secret flag and default (BR-INT-005), **when** a configuration pack sets an INT key that is not in the catalogue, or sets a key flagged secret, **then** the PLT pack validation refuses the pack (PLT-003) and nothing is written.

**Given** the government connector framework (INT-009) is installed, **when** a new e-system adapter plugin is installed and configured, **then** it appears in the connector list and exchanges data without a change to other modules.

**Given** a punch-out connection is configured for a buyer organisation with a shared secret and protocol (cXML or OCI), **when** its purchasing system sends a valid punch-out setup request, **then** Withdrawn (VER-500): now native for cXML — the bundled Misc.PunchOut plugin validates the sender identity and shared secret, starts a PunchOutSession and signs in the contact of the setup request as a customer (found or created by e-mail); verified by AC-INT-012-01-05 and AC-INT-012-01-06; OCI is not native (open item).

**Given** the setup request carries a wrong secret, **when** it is received, **then** Withdrawn (VER-500): now native — the shared secret is compared with the stored hash of the PunchOutIdentity and an error response is returned with no session; verified by AC-INT-012-01-05.

**Given** a punch-out session is open, **when** the buyer returns the cart, **then** Withdrawn (VER-500): now native — the cart is returned as a cXML PunchOutOrderMessage to the session return URL and no order is created; verified by AC-INT-012-01-07.

**Given** the purchasing system later sends a purchase order for a returned cart, **when** it is received, **then** an order is created through IOrderProcessingService.PlaceOrderAsync (CHK-003 override, OVR-REG) for that account and the PO number is stored; a PO for an unknown or expired session is refused.

**Given** the bundled Misc.PunchOut plugin is installed and a PunchOutIdentity is configured with the buyer system identity and shared secret, **when** the purchasing system posts a cXML PunchOutSetupRequest to punchout/setup with a wrong identity or secret, **then** a cXML error response is returned, the attempt is written to the punch-out log and no session starts.

**Given** the same identity and the correct secret, and a contact e-mail in the request, **when** the setup request is processed and the buyer follows the start URL (punchout/start), **then** a PunchOutSession is created for the store with buyer cookie and return URL, the customer with that e-mail is signed in (created if missing) unless the customer is in a role listed in PunchOutSettings.RestrictedCustomerRoleIds, and the storefront opens in punch-out mode.

**Given** a punch-out session is open with items in the cart, **when** the buyer chooses to return the cart (punchout/return), **then** the cart is sent to the session return URL as a cXML PunchOutOrderMessage with the PunchOutSettings.UnitOfMeasureCode, the session data is cleared and no nopCommerce order is created.

**Given** Malawi Post has stated the purpose, data and interface of the MANEPS integration (MG-09) and the adapter is built on INT-009, **when** the data defined for MANEPS is exchanged, **then** it passes through the INT-009 framework with its approval, retry and audit rules — held by MG-09.
**Given** MG-09 is not answered, **when** the MANEPS adapter is configured, **then** no data is sent to MANEPS; the adapter shows as not configured.

**Given** a product uses "manage stock" (ManageInventoryMethod ManageStock) in one warehouse with stock 10, **when** a shopper places an order for 3, **then** the stock becomes 7 and a stock history entry records -3, the new quantity 7 and the order number (native message Admin.StockQuantityHistory.Messages.PlaceOrder).

**Given** a product uses "manage stock by attributes" and one attribute combination has stock 5, **when** a shopper orders 2 of that combination, **then** the combination stock becomes 3 and the history entry carries the combination.

**Given** an order holding 3 units of a product is cancelled, **when** IOrderProcessingService.CancelOrderAsync runs, **then** the 3 units are returned to stock and the history entry uses the native message CancelOrder.

**Given** a seller manages a product of their own, **when** the seller changes its stock quantity, **then** the change is made through an INV-005 adjustment (BR-INV-030); the seller can open only their own products.
basis: REQ-MPC-FR-055; FIT (vendor filter on admin product pages)

criterion: **Given** DisplayStockAvailability and DisplayStockQuantity are on and the stock is 7, above MinStockQuantity, **when** the shopper opens the product page, **then** the page shows the native text Products.Availability.InStockWithQuantity with 7.

**Given** the stock is at or below MinStockQuantity and LowStockActivity is Nothing, **when** the shopper opens the product page, **then** the page shows the native low-stock text (Products.Availability.LowStock or LowStockWithQuantity).

**Given** the stock is 0 and BackorderMode is NoBackorders, **when** the shopper adds the product to the cart, **then** the cart refuses with the native warning ShoppingCart.OutOfStock (or ShoppingCart.QuantityExceedsStock when more than the stock is asked) and the product page shows Products.Availability.OutOfStock.

**Given** an order has just lowered the stock of a product, **when** any shopper requests the product page afterwards, **then** the page shows the lowered quantity on that request; there is no batch or scheduled update of stock figures.
basis: REQ-KTDA-INV-002; FIT (GetProductByIdAsync uses a per-request cache only)

criterion: **Given** BackorderMode is AllowQtyBelow0 and the stock is 0, **when** a shopper orders 2, **then** the order is accepted and the stock becomes -2.

**Given** the user has Inventory.Core.Stock.View, **when** they open the stock history of a product, **then** every change is listed with date, quantity change, new quantity, warehouse and message; for INV documents the message carries the document reference and reason code (BR-INV-031).

**Given** a product uses multiple warehouses with warehouse A stock 5 and warehouse B stock 3 and nothing reserved, **when** a shopper opens the product page, **then** the availability shown is 8, the sum over warehouses of stock minus reserved quantity.

**Given** the same product and no reservations, **when** an order for 6 is placed, **then** ReservedQuantity rises in the warehouse with the most free stock first (A by 5, B by 1); StockQuantity is unchanged until shipment; native writes no history entry at this point.

**Given** units of that order are reserved in warehouse A, **when** the shipment from warehouse A is marked shipped, **then** StockQuantity and ReservedQuantity of warehouse A fall by the shipped quantity and a history entry is written (native message Ship).

**Given** the user has Inventory.Core.Stock.View, **when** they open stock by warehouse for a product, **then** they see per warehouse: stock, reserved, available, quantity in transit and the total; quantity in transit comes from INV-007 transfers when INV-007 (P2) is delivered and is 0 before that.
**Given** an administrator creates or edits a warehouse, **when** the code is empty or already used by another warehouse, **then** the save is refused with message Inv.WarehouseCodeDuplicate.
**Given** the latitude is outside -90 to 90 or the longitude outside -180 to 180, **when** the warehouse is saved, **then** the save is refused with message Inv.CoordinatesInvalid.

**Given** a valid code and coordinates are entered, **when** the warehouse is saved, **then** they are stored in WarehouseExtension, shown in the warehouse list and available to SRC-004, LOG-002 and LOG-008 through IC-INV-05.

**Given** warehouses A and B have coordinates and stock of a product, **when** LOG-002 chooses a distance band or LOG-008 chooses the nearest warehouse for an order line, **then** LOG reads the code and coordinates of A and B through IC-INV-05 (read only); a warehouse without coordinates is returned without them and LOG applies its own fallback (BR-LOG-011).

**Given** NotifyAdminForQuantityBelow is 5 and the stock is 6, **when** an order for 2 is placed (stock 4), **then** the native email QuantityBelow.StoreOwnerNotification is sent; the email is sent only when stock goes down and ends strictly below the level.

**Given** the product belongs to seller V and V set NotifyAdminForQuantityBelow, **when** the stock falls below it through an order, **then** the native email QuantityBelow.VendorNotification is sent to seller V.
basis: REQ-MPC-FR-055; FIT (native since 4.80/4.90, unchanged in 5.00.1: QuantityBelow.VendorNotification)

criterion: **Given** a seller opens the inventory section of one of their own products, **when** they change NotifyAdminForQuantityBelow, MinStockQuantity or LowStockActivity, **then** the values are saved for that product only; the seller cannot open another seller's product.

**Given** MinStockQuantity is 10 and the available stock is 10, **when** the user with Reports.LowStock opens the low-stock report, **then** the product is listed (available stock at or below MinStockQuantity); a seller sees only their own products.

**Given** LowStockActivity is DisableBuyButton, **when** the available stock falls to MinStockQuantity, **then** the buy and wishlist buttons are disabled; they are enabled again when stock rises above MinStockQuantity only if CatalogSettings.PublishBackProductWhenCancellingOrders is on.

**Given** an INV adjustment, receipt, transfer or count lowers the stock below NotifyAdminForQuantityBelow, **when** the INV movement is applied, **then** the same native low-stock emails are sent and the same LowStockActivity is applied as for an order (BR-INV-032).

**Given** the cart hold is enabled for the client, the hold window is set and a product has available stock 5 with no holds, **when** shopper A adds 2 to the cart, **then** after the cart line is saved, an InventoryHold of 2 for shopper A is created with expiry time now plus the hold window by the INV consumer of EntityInsertedEvent / EntityUpdatedEvent<ShoppingCartItem>; the stock others can add is 3; native stock is unchanged (BR-INV-021); if the consumer fails no hold exists and the native stock check at placement still applies.
basis: D; FC-M26-002; FIT (ShoppingCartService.cs:1648, 1706 publish entity events); Proposed (consumer)

criterion: **Given** shopper A holds 2 of a product with available stock 5, **when** shopper B tries to add 4, **then** the native stock check passes (4 is not more than 5), so the INV-004 cart check provider (IC-CHK-01) adds the warning Inv.HeldByOthers showing 3 and the cart refuses the item; the provider is called by the CHK-003 IShoppingCartService override from GetShoppingCartItemWarningsAsync (BR-CHK-015, decision OVR-REG); INV does not override IShoppingCartService.
basis: D; FIT (ShoppingCartService.cs:427, 1141; native add to cart and cart update call GetShoppingCartItemWarningsAsync); OVR-REG

criterion: **Given** shopper A holds 2 of a product with available stock 5 and shopper B has 4 in the cart without a hold, **when** B confirms the order, **then** the same provider runs in the placement cart check (OrderProcessingService calls GetShoppingCartItemWarningsAsync before payment) and the order is refused with Inv.HeldByOthers; A's own holds never count against A (BR-INV-021).

**Given** shopper A has items in the cart, **when** A opens checkout (CheckoutController Index or OnePageCheckout), **then** a hold is created or renewed for every cart line that manages stock, with expiry time now plus the checkout hold window, by an INV action filter on Nop.Web CheckoutController Index and OnePageCheckout [GET].

**Given** a hold has passed its expiry time, **when** any availability check runs or the release task runs, **then** the hold is not counted any more and is set Released; the line stays in shopper A's cart and is checked again against stock at order placement.

**Given** shopper A holds stock, **when** A places the order, **then** native stock is lowered at placement and A's holds for those products are set Converted by an OrderPlacedEvent consumer; if the consumer fails, the holds still end at their expiry time (BR-INV-021).
**Given** a product does not manage stock or allows backorders, **when** it is added to the cart or checkout starts, **then** no hold is created.

**Given** an order is placed with payment method M, and M has a payment window, a reminder count and a reminder interval set, **when** the order is still unpaid (PaymentStatus Pending) when a reminder is due, **then** INV-004 asks TRK-005 to send the reminder (IC-TRK-04 SendEvent with event code Inv.UnpaidOrderReminder, registered by INV at installation through RegisterEventCode); the content carries the pay-again link of PAY-011; channels and TRK-006 opt-outs are applied by TRK (BR-TRK-020); the count of reminders sent is recorded; no reminder is sent after the order is paid, authorised or cancelled.

**Given** the payment window of method M has expired for an order and the configured action for M is Cancel, **when** the unpaid-order task processes the order, **then** under ILocker key 'pay-order-{OrderId}' the task re-reads the order; if PaymentStatus is still Pending, no PaymentTransaction of the order is Successful or Authorized (IC-INV-02) and the order has no shipment, it calls IOrderProcessingService.CancelOrderAsync(order, notifyCustomer: true); the stock is returned (native message CancelOrder), the native OrderCancelled.CustomerNotification is sent and the watch becomes Cancelled (AUD-INV-004).

**Given** the payment window has expired and the action is Cancel, but a PaymentTransaction is Successful or Authorized, or PaymentStatus is no longer Pending, **when** the task re-reads the order under the lock, **then** the order is not cancelled and the watch becomes Closed; nothing else changes.

**Given** the payment window has expired and the action is Cancel, the payment guard passes but the order has a shipment, **when** the task processes the order, **then** the order is not cancelled; the watch becomes Flagged with reason "shipment exists" and appears in the unpaid-order list.

**Given** the payment window has expired and the action for M is Flag, **when** the task processes the order, **then** the watch becomes Flagged, an order note is added and the order appears in the unpaid-order list; stock and order status do not change.

**Given** the payment window has expired and the action for M is Remind, **when** the task processes the order, **then** a final reminder is sent and the watch becomes Expired; the order is not cancelled and stays payable.

**Given** the order's payment method has no payment window configured (for example cash on delivery, letter of credit or on-account), **when** the task runs, **then** the order is ignored; no reminder, flag or cancellation happens (BR-INV-020).

**Given** the user has Inventory.Core.UnpaidOrders.CreateEditDelete, **when** they open the unpaid-order list, **then** flagged orders are shown with payment method, amount, age and reminders sent; the user can release the order (cancel under the same guard as the task) or dismiss the flag with a mandatory reason; every action is audited (AUD-INV-004).
**Given** the user has Inventory.Core.Stock.View, **when** they open the holds of a product, **then** every active hold is listed with customer, quantity, source (cart or checkout) and expiry time.

**Given** product P has active holds and CAT raises Listing.Withdrawn for P (CAT-024), **when** the INV consumer receives the event, **then** it only enqueues a release job for P; the hold-release task then sets every Active hold of P to Released; cart lines are not removed by INV and the native cart warning ShoppingCart.ProductUnpublished refuses P at placement.
basis: D (CAT-024); FIT (consumers swallow exceptions; ShoppingCartService.cs:355); Proposed (job)

criterion: **Given** shopper A holds 2 of a product with available stock 5 and INV-004 is registered with CHK-003 as the replacer of the native warnings ShoppingCart.OutOfStock and ShoppingCart.QuantityExceedsStock (IC-CHK-01), **when** shopper B tries to add 7, **then** the native check produces ShoppingCart.QuantityExceedsStock with 5; INV-004 replaces exactly that warning with Inv.HeldByOthers showing 3, so B sees one stock warning; when no other customer holds the product the native warning is kept unchanged (BR-CHK-015, BR-INV-021).

**Given** the INV-004 unpaid-order watch is installed for a client, **when** the client configuration is applied or validated (PLT-003), **then** the native 5.00 automatic cancellation stays off for every store (OrderSettings.AutoCancelEnabled false; the native task "Auto-cancel unpaid orders" then skips the store), and a pack that switches it on fails validation (BR-INV-023); reason: the native task cancels every Pending or Processing order whose PaymentStatus is Pending after one delay per store (AutoCancelDelay minutes, AutoCancelIgnoredPaymentMethods), without the pay-order lock, the PaymentTransaction check (IC-INV-02), the shipment check or the Remind and Flag actions of BR-INV-020, so it could cancel an order whose payment succeeds at the same moment.
basis: D; INV-HOLD; FIT (Libraries/Nop.Services/Orders/AutoCancelOrdersTask.cs:56-122; Libraries/Nop.Core/Domain/Orders/OrderSettings.cs:184-204; OrderProcessingService.CanCancelOrder, OrderProcessingService.cs:2375-2383; Libraries/Nop.Services/Installation/InstallRequiredData.cs:3582-3591); VER-500

criterion: **Given** the INV-004 unpaid-order reminder is configured for a client, **when** the client configuration is applied or validated (PLT-003), **then** the native 5.00 pending-order reminder stays off (ReminderSettings.PendingOrdersEnabled false; templates Reminders.PendingOrderFollowUp1 and 2 inactive), so a buyer never receives both reminders (BR-INV-023); reason: the native reminder sends at most two emails per order, only to customers with an email address, with one delay per template and not per payment method, and not through TRK-005.

**Given** the user has Inventory.Core.Adjustments.Request and a single-warehouse product has stock 10, **when** they submit -2 with reason Damage and the change is below the approval threshold, **then** the adjustment is Applied at once: IProductService.AdjustInventoryAsync is called with -2 and a message holding the adjustment reference and reason (BR-INV-031); the stock becomes 8; the INV record keeps the requester, reason and note (AUD-INV-001).
**Given** no reason code is chosen, **when** the adjustment is submitted, **then** it is refused with message Inv.AdjustmentReasonRequired.

**Given** a multi-warehouse product and warehouse A are chosen, **when** an adjustment of +5 is applied, **then** StockQuantity of warehouse A rises by 5 through UpdateProductWarehouseInventoryAsync and a history entry is written through AddStockQuantityHistoryEntryAsync for warehouse A; ReservedQuantity is unchanged (BR-INV-034).
basis: FIT (AdjustInventoryAsync changes reservations, not stock, for multi-warehouse products)

criterion: **Given** the product does not allow backorders and the adjustment would take available stock below 0, **when** it is submitted, **then** it is refused with message Inv.AdjustmentBelowZero.

**Given** the size of the change is above the approval threshold, **when** it is submitted, **then** it becomes Requested, the stock does not change, users with Inventory.Core.Adjustments.Approve are notified and the requester sees message Inv.AdjustmentNeedsApproval.
**Given** an adjustment is Requested, **when** the requester tries to approve it, **then** the approval is refused with message Inv.CannotApproveOwn (BR-INV-033).

**Given** an adjustment is Requested, **when** another user with Inventory.Core.Adjustments.Approve approves it, **then** the stock changes as for an applied adjustment and the record becomes Applied with the approver (AUD-INV-001).
**Given** an adjustment is Requested, **when** the approver rejects it with a reason, **then** the record becomes Rejected and the stock does not change.

**Given** a user with only Catalog.ProductsCreateEditDelete changes a stock quantity on the native product edit page, bulk edit grid or attribute-combination popup, **when** the page is posted, **then** an INV action filter refuses the post before it is saved, shows message Inv.UseStockAdjustment and writes AUD-INV-002; posts that do not change a stock quantity are saved as normal (BR-INV-030).
basis: FIT (ProductController Edit, BulkEditSave, ProductAttributeCombinationEditPopup; bulk edit writes no history)

criterion: **Given** a user without Inventory.Core.Adjustments.Approve posts a product Excel import, **when** the import is posted, **then** the INV action filter refuses it with message Inv.UseStockAdjustment; a user with the permission can import and the native history message ImportProduct.Edit records each stock change.

**Given** an INV adjustment brings stock from 0 or below to above 0, **when** it is applied, **then** native back-in-stock notifications are sent as the native product edit does, and BR-INV-032 is applied.

**Given** a buyer accepted an ORD-006 partial-supply proposal, so the unavailable quantities were removed from the order without returning stock, **when** the seller (own products) or warehouse staff find that the physical stock differs from the platform figure, **then** they post an adjustment with a reason code through IC-INV-01 under the normal approval threshold; INV makes no automatic stock movement for partial supply.

**Given** RET-004 restocks a returned unit, **when** RET posts IC-INV-01 PostMovement with reason Return and the lot or serial number where tracked, **then** the movement is Applied without approval (document-backed, BR-INV-033); the history message carries the return reference (BR-INV-031).

**Given** an open purchase order exists (received from the ERP through INV-012 or entered by staff) for warehouse W, **when** staff record a receipt of some or all lines and post it, **then** the accepted quantity of each line is added to stock in W through the adjustment service (IC-INV-01, reason Receipt, no approval: the receipt is the document, BR-INV-040); each line's received quantity is updated and the purchase order becomes PartiallyReceived or Received (SM-INV-04); AUD-INV-006.

**Given** no purchase order exists, **when** staff try to record a receipt, **then** it is refused with message Inv.ReceiptWithoutPo unless the client setting allows receipts without a purchase order; such a receipt is posted as an INV-005 adjustment with reason Receipt and follows its approval threshold.
**Given** a line receives fewer units than ordered, **when** the receipt is posted, **then** the shortage is recorded on the line as a discrepancy and the purchase-order line stays open for the rest.

**Given** some received units are damaged, **when** the receipt is posted with the damaged quantity, **then** the damaged quantity is not added to stock and is recorded as a discrepancy with reason Damaged.
**Given** a line receives more units than the open quantity plus the over-receipt tolerance, **when** the receipt is posted, **then** it is refused with message Inv.OverReceipt.

**Given** a bin location is entered for a line, **when** the receipt is posted, **then** the location (zone, aisle, rack, shelf, bin) is written to the LOG-009 ProductShelfLocation row of that product and warehouse, which LOG pick lists read; INV keeps no shelf-location table of its own.

**Given** inspection is required for the product's category (setting), **when** the receipt is recorded, **then** the line waits as AwaitingInspection and nothing is added to stock; when quality staff record Passed the accepted quantity is posted; a Failed quantity is recorded as a discrepancy.

**Given** the product is lot-tracked (INV-009) or serial-tracked (INV-010), **when** the receipt is posted, **then** the lot number with manufacture and expiry dates, or one serial number per unit, is required (messages Inv.LotRequired, Inv.SerialCountMismatch).

**Given** a transfer of 4 units of a multi-warehouse product from A to B is Draft and A has 4 available, **when** staff dispatch it, **then** StockQuantity of A falls by 4 (history entry with the transfer reference), the transfer becomes InTransit with 4 units in transit, and the in-transit units are not counted as available anywhere (SM-INV-05).
**Given** warehouse A has less available stock than the transfer quantity, **when** staff dispatch it, **then** the dispatch is refused with message Inv.TransferInsufficientStock.
**Given** a transfer is InTransit, **when** B records receipt of all units, **then** StockQuantity of B rises by 4 (history entry with the transfer reference) and the transfer becomes Received.

**Given** a transfer is InTransit, **when** B records receipt of fewer units than sent, **then** B receives what arrived, the transfer becomes ReceivedWithDiscrepancy and the missing units become an INV-005 adjustment request with reason Lost in transit.

**Given** the product does not use multiple warehouses, **when** staff try to add it to a transfer, **then** it cannot be added: a single-warehouse product has one Product.WarehouseId and no stock per warehouse.
**Given** a transfer is Draft, **when** staff cancel it, **then** it becomes Cancelled and no stock changes.
**Given** a transfer changes status, **when** the change is saved, **then** user, time and quantities are recorded (AUD-INV-005).

**Given** a count plan exists with a selection (warehouse, category, ABC class from INV-013 or product list) and a frequency, **when** the plan is due, **then** the count task creates a count with one line per product and warehouse and records the system quantity at that moment (SM-INV-06).
**Given** blind counting is on, **when** a counter opens a count, **then** the system quantity is not shown on the count sheet.

**Given** counted quantities are entered for all lines, **when** the count is submitted, **then** each line shows the variance = counted quantity - (system quantity at creation + net movements recorded in stock history since then).
**Given** a line variance is above the recount threshold, **when** the count is submitted, **then** the line is sent for recount before posting.

**Given** a submitted count has lines with variance not zero, **when** it is posted, **then** each variance becomes an adjustment with reason Count variance through the adjustment service and follows the INV-005 approval threshold; lines with zero variance are closed (BR-INV-060); AUD-INV-007.
**Given** a plan of type Full is due for the selected products, **when** the count is created, **then** every selected product in every warehouse that holds it is in the count.

**Given** a product is set as lot-tracked (only products with ManageInventoryMethod ManageStock), **when** stock is received (INV-006), **then** each receipt line needs a lot number, manufacture date and expiry date (message Inv.LotRequired) and the lot quantity in that warehouse rises by the accepted quantity.

**Given** a product uses "manage stock by attributes", **when** an administrator tries to set it lot-tracked, **then** it is refused: the native cart checks combination stock directly and not GetTotalStockQuantityAsync, so unsellable lots could not be excluded.

**Given** a quality result Failed is recorded for a lot, **when** it is saved, **then** the lot becomes Blocked; its quantity is no longer sellable because the INV sellable-stock provider (IC-INV-04), called by the CAT-002 IProductService override of GetTotalStockQuantityAsync (decision OVR-REG), subtracts the quantity of lots that are Blocked, Expired, Recalled or in Quarantine (BR-INV-071); AUD-INV-008.
**Given** a custody event (holder, from, to, note) is recorded for a lot, **when** it is saved, **then** it is added to the lot's custody chain; earlier custody events cannot be edited or deleted.

**Given** an order line for a lot-tracked product is shipped, **when** staff create the shipment (Admin OrderController.AddShipment [POST]), **then** before the action runs, an INV action filter calls IC-INV-07 Capture, which requires lots for the shipped quantity (pre-filled by FEFO, INV-011) and refuses lots that are not Released (message Inv.LotNotSellable), and on refusal nothing is saved; after the action has saved the shipment and its items, the filter calls IC-INV-07 Confirm, which writes LotAllocation rows linking lot, shipment item, order and customer and lowers the lot quantities (BR-INV-070).
basis: D; FIT ( order events; OrderController.cs:2024-2032); Proposed (capture at shipment)

criterion: **Given** quality staff recall a lot, **when** they confirm the recall, **then** the lot becomes Recalled, its remaining stock stops being sellable and a list of every order, customer, quantity and shipment date for that lot is produced and exportable.

**Given** LOG creates a shipment for a packed line of a lot-tracked product (AC-LOG-009-03-03), **when** LOG calls IC-INV-07 Capture, inserts the shipment and its items, then calls Confirm, **then** Capture applies the same checks as the admin path (Inv.LotRequired, Inv.LotNotSellable) and on refusal LOG saves nothing; when a shipment guard (IC-ORD-11) refuses the insert or the insert fails, LOG calls Cancel and the capture becomes Cancelled with no lot quantity change (SM-INV-10).

**Given** a shipment item of a lot- or serial-tracked product is saved by a path that did not call IC-INV-07 Confirm (for example an API write or a third-party plugin), **when** the INV consumer of EntityInsertedEvent<ShipmentItem> runs, **then** it only enqueues a check; the check lists the item as a capture exception (BR-INV-070, AUD-INV-012) and a user with Inventory.Core.Lots.CreateEditDelete records the lots or serial numbers through IC-INV-07 for that item; the shipment is not blocked.
basis: FIT (ShipmentService.cs:307 inserts through IRepository.InsertAsync, which publishes EntityInsertedEvent; consumers swallow exceptions); Proposed

criterion: **Given** a lot-tracked product, **when** the reconciliation task runs, **then** the sum of Released and unsellable lot quantities per warehouse is compared with native stock plus quantities placed but not yet shipped; any difference is listed as an exception (BR-INV-070).

**Given** a product is set as serial-tracked (ManageStock only), **when** a receipt of 3 units is posted (INV-006), **then** exactly 3 distinct serial numbers are required (message Inv.SerialCountMismatch) and each becomes InStock in that warehouse.

**Given** a shipment of 3 units of a serial-tracked product is created, **when** staff enter the serial numbers, **then** IC-INV-07 Capture requires exactly 3 distinct serial numbers in status InStock and not in another open capture; after the shipment items are saved, Confirm sets each to Shipped and links it to the shipment item, order and customer (SM-INV-08).
**Given** a serial number is unknown or not InStock, **when** it is entered on a shipment, **then** it is refused with message Inv.SerialNotAvailable.
**Given** the user has Inventory.Core.Stock.View, **when** they search a serial number, **then** product, order, customer, shipment date and the serial's event history are shown.
**Given** a returned unit is restocked through RET, **when** the restock is posted, **then** its serial number becomes InStock again with a Returned event.
**Given** the reconciliation task runs, **when** InStock serial numbers of a product differ from its native stock, **then** the difference is listed as an exception.

**Given** a product has lot L1 expiring before lot L2, both Released, **when** a shipment is created, **then** the lot selection is pre-filled from L1 first (FEFO); staff may change it only to another Released lot.

**Given** a lot reaches its expiry date, **when** the daily expiry task runs, **then** the lot becomes Expired and its quantity is excluded from sellable stock by the INV sellable-stock provider (IC-INV-04) to the CAT-002 GetTotalStockQuantityAsync override (BR-INV-071); when sellable stock reaches 0 the native out-of-stock behaviour and LowStockActivity apply.
**Given** the near-expiry window is set, **when** a Released lot enters the window, **then** the lot is flagged on the near-expiry list and stock staff are notified once.

**Given** an Expired lot is disposed of, **when** staff post an adjustment with reason Expiry for the lot, **then** native stock and the lot quantity fall by the same amount through the adjustment service.

**Given** the connector is configured and stock levels flow inbound for a warehouse, **when** the ERP sends a stock level for a SKU in that warehouse, **then** the INV-012 connector, built on the INT-005 framework (IC-INT-03 PullChanges), posts the difference from platform stock through IC-INV-01 with reason ERP sync and the external message ID in the history message: IProductService.AdjustInventoryAsync for a single-warehouse product, UpdateProductWarehouseInventoryAsync with a history entry for a multi-warehouse product (BR-INV-034); it is exempt from the approval threshold and audited (AUD-INV-010).

**Given** movements flow outbound, **when** a stock movement is committed on the platform (placement, cancellation, shipment, adjustment, receipt, transfer, count), **then** an outbound message with channel "stock sync" is written to the single INT-004 outbox through IC-INT-09 Enqueue (the INV consumer only enqueues) and the INT delivery task sends it through the INV-012 connector (IC-INV-03); it becomes Delivered when the connector reports the ERP acknowledgement (SM-INT-01); INV keeps no outbound queue of its own (BR-INV-090, BR-INT-015).
**Given** a message with an external message ID that was already applied arrives again, **when** it is processed, **then** it is applied once only (BR-INV-090, BR-INT-021).

**Given** the same SKU and warehouse changed on both sides since the last sync, **when** the sync runs, **then** the master of record set for that data type (BR-INT-020) wins and the conflict is listed for review with both values.

**Given** valuation is enabled, **when** the valuation schedule runs, **then** quantity and value per SKU and warehouse are sent, with value = quantity x Product.ProductCost unless the client sets another method.

**Given** purchase triggers are enabled, **when** available stock of a product reaches MinStockQuantity, **then** a purchase trigger with SKU, warehouse and quantity on hand is sent to the ERP once until stock rises above the level again.

**Given** sending an outbound stock message fails, **when** the INT-004 retry policy applies, **then** it is retried up to the configured number of attempts (RetryWaiting, SM-INT-01); after the last attempt it becomes DeadLettered in the INT-004 outbox, the INT dead-letter notification is sent (event code Int.Core.MessageDeadLettered) and a user holding Integrations.Core.Messages.Replay replays or discards it with a reason (AUD-INT-003); no stock message is lost.

**Given** a period is selected, **when** the sell-rate report runs, **then** per product it shows units sold (order lines of orders placed in the period, cancelled orders excluded), average units sold per day, current sellable stock and days of cover = sellable stock / average units per day (blank when nothing was sold).
**Given** daily stock snapshots exist for the period, **when** the stock-out report runs, **then** per product it shows the number of days on which sellable stock was 0 or less.

**Given** the dead-stock window is set, **when** the dead-stock report runs, **then** it lists products with stock above 0 and no units sold within the window, with stock value (stock x Product.ProductCost).
**Given** the ABC cut-offs are set, **when** the ABC report runs for a period, **then** products are put in classes A, B and C by cumulative share of sales value in the period, highest first.

**Given** RPT-001 builds its fast and slow mover or stock-level view for a period, **when** it calls IC-INV-06, **then** INV returns per product and warehouse the daily sellable-stock snapshots, the stock movements by reason (from stock history and INV records) and the current sellable stock (BR-INV-100); INV-013 shows no fast / slow mover or stock-level dashboard of its own.
**Given** a seller opens the INV-013 reports, **when** the data is loaded, **then** only the seller's own products are shown.

**Given** three shipping methods are active and allowed for the shopper's country (ShippingMethodCountryMapping), **when** the shopper reaches the delivery step, **then** all three are listed with name, description, price and expected delivery range, in the configured display order.
**Given** a shipping method is not allowed for the destination country, **when** the shopper reaches the delivery step, **then** that method is not listed.

**Given** a service level has transit days set (rate table TransitDays or LOG-005 standard), **when** its price is shown, **then** the expected delivery range for that level is shown next to it (LOG-005); the service level, price and promised range are stored with the order.

**Given** a rate table by weight and order subtotal is configured for a method, **when** the cart weight or subtotal changes, **then** the delivery charge is recalculated on the next display of the delivery step and of the order summary.
**Given** the LOG-002 fee engine is the active rate method, **when** the shopper reaches the delivery step, **then** the charge comes from the LOG-002 fee rules (BR-LOG-010), not from a fixed amount.

**Given** ShippingSettings.FreeShippingOverXEnabled is on with a value set, **when** the order subtotal reaches the value, **then** the delivery charge is zero for every method and the summary shows free delivery.

**Given** no method is available for the address, **when** the shopper reaches the delivery step, **then** checkout stops with message Log.NoDeliveryAvailable and offers pickup points if any are available (LOG-003).

**Given** a fee table defines a base fee per service level and zone, a weight band component and a rural surcharge, **when** an order for a rural address with a weight in band 2 is quoted, **then** the fee = base (service level, zone) + band-2 component + rural component, using the table version in force (BR-LOG-010, BR-LOG-012).

**Given** a fee table uses distance bands, **when** the origin and the destination both have coordinates (origin warehouse read through IC-INV-05 GetWarehouseLocation; destination LOG-015), **then** the distance band is chosen from the straight-line distance (BR-LOG-011).

**Given** a fee table uses distance bands, **when** the destination has no coordinates, **then** the zone table of the same service level applies; if none exists, the option is not offered and the case is logged (BR-LOG-011).

**Given** a delivery and a pickup option exist for the same service level, **when** the fees are calculated, **then** the pickup option uses the pickup fee table and the outlet's PickupFee, and the delivery option uses the delivery table.

**Given** the location type of the destination area is urban and the urban table differs from the rural table, **when** the fee is calculated, **then** the urban table applies; location type comes from the LOG-004 coverage area (BR-LOG-021).
**Given** the shopper changes the address, cart weight or service level, **when** the delivery step is shown again, **then** the fee is recalculated (dynamic calculation).

**Given** a fee has more than one component, **when** the delivery options and the order summary are shown, **then** each component (base, weight, distance or zone, location type, pickup or delivery) is listed with its amount under label Log.FeeBreakdown, and the components sum to the fee.

**Given** an order is placed, **when** the order is inserted, **then** the quote used (components, table version, service level) is stored against the order (OrderDeliveryQuote) from the selected shipping option; if it cannot be linked, the order is listed in the logistics exceptions view.
basis: Proposed; FIT (SelectedShippingOption generic attribute is reset before OrderPlacedEvent)

criterion: **Given** a new fee table version is saved with a future effective date, **when** an order is placed before that date, **then** the previous version applies and the order records the version used (BR-LOG-012); the change is audited (AUD-LOG-002).
**Given** pickup fees are configured per outlet and per service level, **when** a pickup option is quoted, **then** the pickup fee configured for that outlet and level applies.

**Given** the INT-010 tariff sync delivers rows with an external key and an effective date, **when** the rows are written to the fee tables, **then** they are stored as a fee-table version with that effective date and external key; a row whose external key and effective date already exist replaces the stored row only while no order has used that version, otherwise it is refused and listed in the configuration exceptions list; orders keep the version in force when they were placed (BR-LOG-012).

**Given** a revenue-share rule (fixed or percentage of the delivery fee) exists for a partner and service level, **when** a shipment is assigned to that partner (LOG-021), **then** the partner share and the client share are recorded per shipment, sum to the delivery fee and use the rule version in force at assignment (BR-LOG-013).
**Given** no revenue-share rule exists for the assigned partner, **when** the shipment is assigned, **then** no share is recorded and the shipment appears in the configuration exceptions list.

**Given** an outlet is created as a StorePickupPoint (bundled Pickup.PickupInStore data) with address, OpeningHours, PickupFee, Latitude, Longitude and TransitDays, **when** it is saved, **then** it is stored once in the native table; the LOG outlet extension (capacity flag, closures) references it by StorePickupPointId; no second outlet table is created.

**Given** pickup is allowed (ShippingSettings.AllowPickupInStore) and the LOG outlet provider is active (ActivePickupPointProviderSystemNames), **when** the shopper chooses pickup, **then** outlets of the current store are listed with name, address, opening hours and fee; with DisplayPickupPointsOnMap on they appear on the map.

**Given** an outlet has a closure from date A to date B, **when** a shopper whose expected arrival date (LOG-005) falls between A and B chooses pickup, **then** that outlet is not offered, or is shown disabled with message Log.OutletClosed (BR-LOG-020).
**Given** an outlet is flagged full, **when** a shopper chooses pickup, **then** that outlet is not offered and message Log.OutletFull is shown on the outlet list.

**Given** an outlet's status changes (closure added or ended, capacity flag set or cleared), **when** it is saved, **then** the change is audited (AUD-LOG-011); orders already placed for that outlet are listed for operations follow-up.

**Given** an outlet synchronised by INT-010 is removed in the Malawi Post source system, **when** the outlet sync runs, **then** the StorePickupPoint row is not deleted (it has no active flag); a closure with reason "Removed at source" and no end date is added through the outlet extension, so the outlet is no longer offered (BR-LOG-020) and orders already placed keep their outlet.
basis: see INT-010 (REQ-MPC-FR-349); FIT (StorePickupPoint has no active flag)

criterion: **Given** an administrator links an outlet to the warehouse that supplies it (PickupPointWarehouse), **when** the link is saved, **then** it is stored once in the LOG table and used for outlet availability (IC-LOG-06), SRC-004 nearby pickup and SRC-018 pickup windows; the change is audited (AUD-LOG-011).

**Given** an administrator sets the outlet flag "accepts returns" on an outlet, **when** it is saved, **then** the outlet is returned by IC-LOG-06 GetOutlets with the returns filter, which RET-003 uses to list drop-off outlets for returns; the change is audited (AUD-LOG-011).

**Given** an order is placed with pickup, **when** the order is inserted, **then** the chosen outlet id is stored against the order (OrderOutlet) from the SelectedPickupPoint generic attribute, because the order stores only a copy of the outlet address (Order.PickupAddressId).
basis: FIT (OrderProcessingService.PrepareAndValidateShippingInfoAsync, OrderProcessingService.cs:426-432; IShoppingCartService.ResetCheckoutDataAsync before OrderPlacedEvent, OrderProcessingService.cs:1636-1637; moved from ICustomerService in 5.00)

criterion: **Given** coverage areas are defined by country, region (StateProvince), district (County) and postal-code pattern, each with service levels allowed, outlets serving it and a location type (rural / urban), **when** an area is saved, **then** it is stored with its attributes and audited (AUD-LOG-002).
**Given** the shopper's address is not in any coverage area for service level S, **when** the delivery step is shown, **then** service level S is not listed (BR-LOG-020).
**Given** the shopper's address is in an area served by outlets X and Y only, **when** the shopper chooses pickup, **then** only outlets X and Y are listed.
**Given** no delivery and no pickup option is available, **when** the delivery step is shown, **then** checkout stops with message Log.NoDeliveryAvailable and no order can be placed.

**Given** a ship-enabled product has a list of allowed service levels and outlets (ProductDeliveryOption, for example an e-Government service with a physical output, EGV-004), **when** the shopper reaches the delivery step with that product, **then** only the allowed service levels and outlets are offered for its (sub-)order; with no list, every option allowed by the coverage area applies (BR-LOG-020).

**Given** another module asks whether an item can be delivered to an area or address for a service level (CHK-005 and CHK-011 at checkout, SVC-006 at booking, SRC-004 for the delivery filter) through IC-LOG-06 IsServiceable, **when** the call is made, **then** the answer is computed by BR-LOG-020 exactly as at the delivery step, with the reason when not serviceable (area not covered, seller area, product restriction).

**Given** the Marketplace pack is on and a seller has saved coverage districts, **when** a buyer outside them has that seller's items in the cart, **then** delivery is not offered for that seller's (sub-)order and message Log.SellerAreaNotCovered names the items concerned.

**Given** a seller's coverage is enforced at the delivery step, **when** the order is submitted, **then** checkout validation re-checks coverage before placement so an address changed in between is refused (CHK-003).

**Given** a delivery standard defines, per origin, destination area and service level, transit days (minimum and maximum) and the days on which the transport link departs; the cut-off time, handling time and working-day calendar of the service level are those of ORD-011 ServiceLevel, **when** the standard is saved, **then** it is stored and audited (AUD-LOG-002); LOG stores no cut-off, handling time or calendar of its own (one source, ORD-011).

**Given** an order is quoted before the ORD-011 cut-off time of its service level on a working day of the ORD-011 calendar, **when** the EDT is calculated, **then** the dispatch day is today; otherwise the next working day (BR-LOG-030).

**Given** the transport link departs only on certain days, **when** the EDT is calculated, **then** the dispatch day moves to the next departure day before transit days are added (connectivity constraint, BR-LOG-030).

**Given** the EDT is calculated, **when** it is presented, **then** the earliest and latest dates are shown with message Log.EdtRange at the delivery step (CHK-014), on the order and on the tracking page (TRK-001); non-working days are skipped.
**Given** no standard exists for the route, **when** the EDT is requested, **then** the native transit days of the rate or pickup point are used if set; otherwise message Log.EdtUnavailable is shown.
**Given** an order is placed, **when** the order is inserted, **then** the promised range is stored with the order and used by LOG-018 for on-time measurement.

**Given** CHK-014 requests an estimate through IC-CHK-03 for a shipping option, or for a pickup point, with the address and cart, **when** LOG-005 answers (IC-LOG-06 GetDeliveryEstimate), **then** it returns the earliest and latest date by BR-LOG-030 (for a pickup point: the date from which the order can be collected), or none when neither a standard nor native transit days exist.

**Given** delivery standards exist and the precompute task runs (interval: setting, default not stated), **when** it finishes, **then** a delivery window per product and district (and a store default window when no district is chosen) is stored in DeliveryWindowCache; SRC-018 listing cards and the SRC-004 delivery filter read it through IC-LOG-06 GetDeliveryWindow without any shipping-rate call per card.

**Given** a DHL plugin built for nopCommerce 5.00 is licensed and installed (5.00 build not verifiable from source, VER-500), or the custom fallback adapter on LOG-021 is built, **when** the plugin is configured with KTDA's DHL account, **then** it appears as a carrier in LOG-021 and, if enabled for checkout, as a rate method (IShippingRateComputationMethod.GetShippingOptionsAsync).

**Given** a shipment is assigned to DHL, **when** staff book it, **then** a DHL booking is created, the DHL waybill number is set as the shipment tracking number (ShipmentTrackingNumberSetEvent) and the DHL label is stored for printing (LOG-007).

**Given** DHL reports a tracking event through its API (push or polling), **when** the adapter receives it, **then** it is passed to the TRK-002 hub with the DHL status code, which maps it to the common event list; the timeline shows it.

**Given** the licensed plugin does not implement booking, label or event push, **when** the gap is found in the VER-500 plugin test, **then** the missing operations are reported as NotSupported in its capability record (IC-LOG-01) and are provided by the fallback adapter or done manually.

**Given** a shipment exists, **when** a label is generated, **then** it shows sender, recipient, weight, service level, the shipment identifier and the tracking number as a barcode in the configured symbology; for a carrier booking it is the carrier's label (IC-LOG-01 GetLabel).
**Given** the shipment is international postal and has no tracking number, **when** the label is generated, **then** an S10 identifier is assigned first (LOG-020) and printed as the barcode.
**Given** a digital postcode or address alias is stored for the address (LOG-015), **when** the label is generated, **then** it is printed on the label.
**Given** a label is printed, **when** its barcode is scanned with the client's postal scanner in acceptance testing, **then** the scanner returns the identifier printed on the label (test T-LOG-04).

**Given** a network printer address is configured for the warehouse or outlet, **when** staff choose network print, **then** the label is sent in the printer language of the configured printer (ZPL for Zebra-type printers); otherwise a PDF or PNG is produced.

**Given** label and packing-slip templates are configured, **when** a seller prints for selected own orders, **then** packing slips (native PrintPackagingSlipsToPdfAsync) and labels are produced only for shipments of that seller (native vendor filter).

**Given** RET-003 needs a return label for a ReturnShipment (not a native Shipment), **when** it requests the label with the return reference, sender (shopper or outlet) and destination, **then** the label is produced by the same templates and barcode rules with the return tracking reference as the barcode (the carrier label when IC-LOG-01 BookReturn returned one) and stored as a Download referenced by the ReturnShipment; the reference is the one RET-003 registered with TRK-002 (IC-TRK-01 RegisterExternalReference), so scans of the label are applied to the return.

**Given** the fulfilment model of a line is merchant-fulfilled, client-fulfilled or third-party (BR-LOG-060), **when** the order is paid or, for COD and on-account orders, placed, **then** a fulfilment task is created for the party of that model and appears in its queue (seller dashboard ORD-005, warehouse queue LOG-009, or the partner booking LOG-021).
**Given** a seller opted in to client fulfilment (SEL-018), **when** that seller's line is allocated, **then** the model is client-fulfilled unless the product overrides it (BR-LOG-060).

**Given** two warehouses hold enough stock for the line (ProductWarehouseInventory) and both have coordinates (read through IC-INV-05 GetWarehouseLocation), **when** the line is allocated, **then** the warehouse nearest to the destination is chosen (BR-LOG-061).

**Given** no single warehouse holds enough stock, **when** the line is allocated, **then** the line is split across warehouses in order of distance, or flagged for manual allocation when the client disallows splits (setting, default not stated).

**Given** a user with Logistics.Core.Fulfilment.CreateEditDelete changes an allocation, **when** they save it with a reason, **then** the task moves to the new party or warehouse and the change is audited (AUD-LOG-004).

**Given** a KTDA fulfilment workflow (ADM-002) is started from a queued order event and reaches an allocation, pick, pack or dispatch step, **when** the step runs, **then** it calls the LOG fulfilment service (IC-LOG-07) with the task and acting user; LOG applies its rules and state model (SM-LOG-01) and returns the result; the workflow never changes order, shipment or task state itself (BR-LOG-190).
