**Given** a seller uploads proof through the PAY seller endpoint, **when** the file is received, **then** the PAY endpoint checks the file through IC-ADM-08 CheckUpload with the upload context "offline payment proof", which PAY registers at installation through IC-ADM-08 RegisterUploadContext (own endpoint), before it stores the file through IDownloadService; a refused file is not stored and the ADM message key is returned; PAY keeps no type check of its own; the OrderNote is saved with DisplayToCustomer on, so the buyer opens the proof through native DownloadController.GetOrderNoteFile, which serves it only to the order's customer.
basis: Proposed; see ADM-008 (BR-ADM-060); FIT (GetOrderNoteFile checks Order.CustomerId)

criterion: **Given** a provisioning request names the client code, the product release version and the client pack set (global, country, vertical, client), **when** the provisioning pipeline runs, **then** two installations are created, live and test, each with its own database, its own App_Data/appsettings.json connection string, its own App_Data folder (plugins.json, DataProtectionKeys) and the same product release (BR-PLT-001, BR-PLT-003).

**Given** the installations exist, **when** nopCommerce installation completes on each, **then** only the plugins in the release plugin folder that are not listed in InstallationConfig.DisabledPlugins are installed (native installer behaviour), then the PLT plugin applies the client pack set through the pack loader (PLT-003) and records the applied pack set.

**Given** a new client is provisioned, **when** provisioning completes, **then** the test instance reaches status Active first; the live instance cannot be set Active until a UAT sign-off (reference, signed by, date) is recorded on it; an attempt is refused with message Plt.InstanceNotSignedOff (BR-PLT-002).

**Given** any provisioning step fails, **when** the pipeline stops, **then** the instance status becomes ProvisioningFailed, the failed step and the resources already created are reported to the platform team, and no live instance is set Active.
**Given** the test instance is created, **when** it is used, **then** it holds no production customer, order or payment data and uses its own provider credentials, entered per instance (BR-PLT-013).

**Given** a live instance is ready for go-live, **when** the go-live checklist is run, **then** each item is recorded as passed or failed with evidence, and the instance cannot be set Active while an item is failed (BR-PLT-004): HTTPS on every store (Store.SslEnabled true); forwarded headers set when TLS ends at a proxy (HostingConfig.UseProxy, ForwardedProtoHeaderName, ForwardedForHeaderName, KnownProxies or KnownNetworks); TLS versions and ciphers; encryption at rest for database, files and backups; web application firewall and DDoS protection in front; an application database login with insert and select only on audit tables (SEC-004); hosting region per DP-01; DistributedCacheConfig.Enabled when more than one web node.
basis: Proposed (SEC hosting items); FIT (Store.SslEnabled; HostingConfig; DistributedCacheConfig)

criterion: **Given** an instance is Active, **when** the platform team sets it Suspended with a reason, **then** StoreInformationSettings.StoreClosed is set true for every store, so the storefront shows the native store-closed page except to users holding PublicStore.AccessClosedStore; the client contact is notified; audited (AUD-PLT-001).
**Given** an instance is Suspended, **when** it is set Active again, **then** StoreClosed returns to the value recorded before suspension; the client contact is notified; audited (AUD-PLT-001).

**Given** an instance is Active or Suspended, **when** the platform team sets it Archived, **then** a final backup is taken and verified (PLT-016), the application is stopped and the database is kept for the archive period (setting, default not stated); the client contact is notified.

**Given** an instance is Archived, **when** the platform team restores it, **then** the database and App_Data are restored from the archive backup, the status becomes Restored and then Active after a smoke test passes; any other transition is rejected (SM-PLT-01).

**Given** two clients are provisioned, **when** their configuration is inspected, **then** each installation has its own database connection string, App_Data folder, data-protection keys and media storage; none of these is shared between clients (BR-PLT-003).
basis: D; FC-M09-002; FIT (DataSettingsManager: one connection string per installation)

criterion: **Given** two client instances use the same Redis or SQL Server distributed-cache server, **when** the instances are configured, **then** DistributedCacheConfig.InstanceName is unique per instance (the native default "nopCommerce" is never used), so cache keys and locks of one instance are never read by another.

**Given** a client needs a B2B and a B2C storefront, **when** the client is set up, **then** both are stores of the same client installation (PLT-013); stores are never used to separate two clients, because stores share one database and admin users are not limited by store.

**Given** a user account exists in client A, **when** the same e-mail and password are used on client B, **then** sign-in fails on client B unless an account was created there; no customer, order or price of client A is returned by any page or API of client B.
**Given** the operator cross-client view is used (PLT-014), **when** it is opened, **then** it reads only monitoring data exported by each instance; no instance holds data of another client.

**Given** global, country, vertical and client packs that each state key K, **when** the loader merges them, **then** the client value wins over the vertical value, the vertical value over the country value and the country value over the global value; a key not stated by a higher layer keeps the value of the lower layer (BR-PLT-010).

**Given** the merged result, **when** it is applied, **then** merged shared keys are written as Setting rows with StoreId 0 and store entries as rows with StoreId of the named store; at run time SettingService.LoadSettingAsync returns the store row, else the StoreId 0 row, else the settings-class default; no other layer exists at run time (BR-PLT-011).

**Given** a store entry for key K was applied by the previous pack version and the new pack version no longer states it, **when** the new version is applied, **then** the store row for K is deleted, so the store again uses the StoreId 0 value (BR-PLT-011).
basis: Proposed; FIT (SettingService.SaveSettingOverridablePerStoreAsync deletes store rows the same way)

criterion: **Given** a pack is validated, **when** a setting key is not a property of a known ISettings class (lower-case <ClassName>.<PropertyName>) and not in the key catalogue of an installed product plugin, or a value cannot be converted by the property TypeConverter, **then** validation fails with message Plt.PackKeyUnknown naming the key and nothing is written.
basis: Proposed; FIT (SettingService key format and TypeDescriptor conversion)

criterion: **Given** a pack maps permissions to roles, **when** it is validated, **then** every permission system name must exist in the 5.00 permission set (StandardPermission or a plugin IPermissionConfigManager); a 4.70 name such as ManageProducts, or a 4.90 name removed in 5.00 (ContentManagement.NewsView, NewsCreateEditDelete, PollsView, PollsCreateEditDelete, ForumsCreateEditDelete; news, polls and forums are now the bundled plugins Misc.News, Misc.Polls and Misc.Forums with their own permissions), fails with message Plt.PackPermissionUnknown.
basis: FIT (L1 section 6.1: 5.00 permission model; Libraries/Nop.Services/Security/StandardPermission.cs; Plugins/Nop.Plugin.Misc.News, Nop.Plugin.Misc.Polls, Nop.Plugin.Misc.Forums)

criterion: **Given** a store entry names a store code that does not exist in the instance, **when** the pack is validated, **then** validation fails with message Plt.PackStoreUnknown and nothing is written.
**Given** a pack contains a key on the secret deny list (BR-PLT-013), **when** it is imported, **then** the import is refused with message Plt.PackSecretRefused naming the key.

**Given** a pack contains plugin enablement, **when** it is applied, **then** plugins to install are queued with IPluginService.PreparePluginToInstallAsync and the run ends with message Plt.RestartRequired (installation runs at application start, AppStartedConsumer); store and role limits are written to each plugin's plugin.json through PluginDescriptor.Save; active-provider lists (for example paymentsettings.activepaymentmethodsystemnames) are written as settings (BR-PLT-012).

**Given** the pack holds locale resources, message templates, roles, categories and specification attributes, feature states and ADM workflow and rule definitions, **when** it is applied, **then** each artefact is written through its native or owning service (ILocalizationService.ImportResourcesFromXmlAsync, IMessageTemplateService, IPermissionService.InsertPermissionMappingAsync, ICategoryService, the PLT-022 registry, the ADM-002 and ADM-003 contracts); no artefact is written by direct SQL.

**Given** a validated pack set, **when** it is applied, **then** all database writes run in one TransactionScope under ILocker key 'plt-config-write'; if any write fails none is kept and the run status becomes Failed with message Plt.PackApplyFailed (BR-PLT-015).
basis: Proposed; FIT (EntityRepository bulk writes open INopDataProvider.CreateTransactionScope: TransactionScopeOption.Required, Serializable, async flow enabled, so they join an outer scope — Libraries/Nop.Data/DataProviders/BaseDataProvider.cs:503-533; ILocker.PerformActionWithLockAsync)

criterion: **Given** the database writes are committed and a file write (plugin.json or plugins.json) fails, **when** the loader detects the failure, **then** it restores the files and the database rows from the pre-apply snapshot, sets the run Failed and shows message Plt.PackApplyFailed (BR-PLT-015).

**Given** an apply succeeds, **when** the run completes, **then** the instance records the applied pack set (pack codes, versions, checksums, applied by, applied at) and the setting cache is cleared once at the end (settings are written with clearCache false, then ISettingService.ClearCacheAsync); audited (AUD-PLT-002).
**Given** the same pack set (same checksums) was already applied, **when** it is applied again, **then** nothing is written and the run reports "no changes" (BR-PLT-016).

**Given** a key was changed in the instance after the last apply, so its value differs from the value the last pack wrote, **when** a new pack version that states the key is applied, **then** the run stops before writing and lists each such key with message Plt.PackConflict; for each key the platform team chooses keep the instance value (recorded as a deviation) or take the pack value; audited (AUD-PLT-003).

**Given** a transaction type (ADM-004) has a parameter whose client default comes from the client pack, **when** a client administrator sets a type-level override with a reason, **then** transactions of that type use the override, other types use the client value, and the override is recorded as a deviation with pack value, override value, reason and user (BR-PLT-017).

**Given** a single transaction overrides a parameter of its type, **when** it is saved without a reason, **then** the save is refused with message Plt.OverrideReasonRequired; with a reason it is saved, recorded as a deviation and audited (AUD-PLT-012).

**Given** an override at transaction-type or transaction level names a native setting key (a Setting row), **when** it is saved, **then** it is refused with message Plt.OverrideNotAllowed, because native settings resolve only by store and shared value (BR-PLT-011, BR-PLT-017).

**Given** a pack set names no country pack, or two country packs, **when** it is validated, **then** validation fails with message Plt.PackCountryInvalid and nothing is written; a pack set with exactly one country pack (for example a Kenya or Malawi pack, contents Not stated in source) is applied at the country layer of BR-PLT-010 and its code, version and checksum are recorded with the applied pack set.

**Given** a pack written for nopCommerce 4.90 states a setting key that 5.00 removed or moved (customersettings.phonenumbervalidationuseregex and customersettings.phonenumbervalidationrule are removed; ordersettings.returnrequestsenabled, returnrequestsallowfiles, returnrequestsfilemaximumsize, returnrequestnumbermask and numberofdaysreturnrequestavailable are now returnrequestsettings.*), **when** the pack is validated against a 5.00 instance, **then** validation fails with message Plt.PackKeyUnknown naming each such key and nothing is written; the pack is corrected by dropping the removed keys (5.00 validates phone numbers with libphonenumber when CustomerSettings.PhoneNumberValidationEnabled is on) and renaming the moved keys.

**Given** key K is on the controlled-items list and has a validator (type, range, reference or cross-key rule), **when** an administrator saves a settings page or the All settings grid with an invalid value for K, **then** nothing is written, the page shows message Plt.ConfigInvalid with the key and the reason, and the live value is unchanged.

**Given** key K is controlled, **when** an administrator saves a valid change to K through any admin page (settings pages, All settings SettingUpdate, SettingAdd, SettingDelete, a plugin Configure page), **then** the PLT action filter marks the request as change-controlled and the PLT ISettingService override records the write in a pending change set instead of writing the Setting row; the page shows message Plt.ChangePending; the live value is unchanged (BR-PLT-020).
basis: Proposed; FIT (SettingService InsertSettingAsync, UpdateSettingAsync and DeleteSettingAsync are public virtual and are the only write path; 5.00.1 removed every synchronous ISettingService member, so the override implements async members only — Libraries/Nop.Services/Configuration/ISettingService.cs:27-192; SettingDelete(int id) takes no model, so a ModelReceivedEvent veto cannot cover it)

criterion: **Given** key K is not controlled, **when** an administrator saves it, **then** it is saved natively; the SEC-004 repository decorator records the old and new value (BR-PLT-022).

**Given** the instance role is Test, **when** a valid change to a controlled key is saved, **then** the change set is applied at once after validation, without approval, and is still recorded (BR-PLT-020).

**Given** a change set is pending, **when** the requester or approver opens it, **then** the preview lists, per key, the store or shared scope, the current and new value, the stores that inherit the shared value, and the impact counts returned by any module registered for that key (IC-PLT-03), for example the number of open orders using a payment method.

**Given** a change set of impact level Low is pending, **when** one user holding Platform.Core.ChangeControl.Approve other than the requester approves it, **then** it is applied through the base SettingService under ILocker key 'plt-config-write' and the status becomes Applied; audited (AUD-PLT-004).
**Given** a change set of impact level High is pending, **when** one approver approves it, **then** it stays PendingApproval until a second, different approver approves it (BR-PLT-020).
**Given** the requester tries to approve their own change set, **when** they press approve, **then** the action is refused with message Plt.ApproveOwnChange.

**Given** a change set is approved, **when** the current value of any of its keys differs from the old value recorded in the change set, **then** the change set is not applied, its status becomes Stale and message Plt.ChangeStale is shown (BR-PLT-021).
**Given** an approver rejects a change set, **when** they enter a reason, **then** the change set becomes Rejected, nothing is written and the requester is notified with the reason.

**Given** any setting is written, controlled or not, **when** the write completes, **then** the configuration history shows actor, timestamp, key, store, old value and new value, read from the SEC-004 audit store; applied change sets also show reason and approvers.

**Given** a user with Platform.Core.ChangeControl.View, **when** runs the configuration-change report for a period, **then** all configuration changes in the period are listed with actor, timestamp, key, store, old and new value, reason and approvers, filterable by user, key and store and exportable to a file.

**Given** a module registers a configuration type as controlled through IC-PLT-03, for example PAY risk rules, **when** a rule of that type is enabled or disabled, **then** the change follows the same change-set flow and is shown in the history with old and new values.

**Given** the history of key K shows earlier values, **when** an administrator selects one or more keys and an earlier version and requests rollback, **then** a new change set restoring those values is created and goes through the same validation and approval; nothing is written until it is approved (BR-PLT-023).

**Given** a rollback change set is previewed, **when** a key to be restored is used by in-flight records registered by a module (IC-PLT-03), **then** the preview lists the affected record counts before approval.
**Given** an auditor selects a past date, **when** they open the configuration as of that date, **then** the value of every controlled key at that date is shown, rebuilt from the history.

**Given** two configuration snapshots (two dates in this instance, or an exported pack of another instance), **when** a member of the platform team compares them, **then** keys with different values are listed side by side; selected differences can be copied into a new change set in this instance.

**Given** a user with Platform.Core.Packs.CreateEditDelete, **when** they export the configuration, **then** a pack file is produced holding every exportable artefact of the configuration-pack schema (section 10.1) at client and store layers, store entries keyed by store code, with a manifest (instance code, product release version, export time, checksum); audited (AUD-PLT-006).

**Given** the configuration contains secrets (BR-PLT-013) and instance-bound items (BR-PLT-014), **when** it is exported, **then** secrets are omitted and listed by key only in the manifest as "to be entered"; entity data (customers, orders, products) is not part of the export (data backup is PLT-016).

**Given** an exported pack file, **when** it is imported into another instance, **then** it is validated and applied through the PLT-003 loader (all PLT-003 criteria apply), and the run lists the secrets to be entered in the target instance.
**Given** the pack was exported from a newer product release than the target instance runs, **when** it is imported, **then** the import is refused with message Plt.PackVersionMismatch.

**Given** changes were made and accepted in the test instance, **when** a member of the platform team starts a promotion, **then** the differences between the test export and the live configuration are listed excluding instance-bound items (BR-PLT-014); the selected differences become a change set in the live instance that follows PLT-004 validation and approval.

**Given** client A's configuration is to be the starting point for client B, **when** a clone is requested without a recorded authorisation reference, **then** it is refused with message Plt.CloneNotAuthorised.

**Given** an authorised clone, **when** it is exported from A and applied to B, **then** client-identifying items (store names, URLs, hosts, company details, logos, e-mail accounts, secrets) are excluded and listed for entry, and the result is recorded in B as a client pack derived from A; audited (AUD-PLT-006).
**Given** a client logo is uploaded, **when** it is set for a store, **then** the storefront header shows it for that store (StoreInformationSettings.LogoPictureId, store-overridable).

**Given** the client brand guidelines (logo, colour values, fonts) are supplied, **when** they are entered through the theme settings — the licensed theme plugin admin if the vendor confirms a 5.00 build (open item under VER-500), otherwise a client child theme of DefaultClean whose colour and font values are set in one variables file, **then** every storefront page of the store uses those colours and fonts, with no change to product code.

**Given** two stores of one client, **when** each has its own theme (DefaultStoreTheme stored per store), **then** each storefront shows its own theme; customer theme selection is offered only if AllowCustomerToSelectTheme is on.

**Given** the branding is set, **when** an invoice PDF or a system e-mail is produced, **then** the PDF uses the logo of PdfSettings.LogoPictureId (or the DOC-001 template branding) and the e-mail uses the client header of the message template (TRK-004).

**Given** the client domain points to the instance and a TLS certificate is installed at the hosting layer, **when** the store is configured with Store.Url (https address), Store.Hosts (comma-separated host names) and Store.SslEnabled = true, **then** requests on any listed host resolve to that store and HTTP requests are redirected to HTTPS by the native HttpsRequirement filter.
basis: D; FIT (Store.Url, Store.Hosts, Store.SslEnabled; HttpsRequirementAttribute; StoreService host parsing)

criterion: **Given** TLS ends at a load balancer or reverse proxy, **when** the instance is configured, **then** HostingConfig.UseProxy is true with the forwarded-protocol header set, so a secure request is recognised and no redirect loop occurs.
**Given** Store.SslEnabled is false, **when** a secure request arrives, **then** the native filter redirects it to HTTP; therefore every client store is set SslEnabled = true (BR-PLT-003 checklist).
basis: FIT (HttpsRequirementAttribute: redirects to HTTP when SslEnabled is false)

criterion: **Given** an e-mail account with the client address, display name and SMTP or OAuth2 authentication (EmailAuthenticationMethod Login, GmailOAuth2 or MicrosoftOAuth2) is created and set as default (EmailAccountSettings.DefaultEmailAccountId), **when** a system e-mail is sent, **then** it is sent from that address; a template with its own EmailAccountId uses that account instead.

**Given** SPF, DKIM and DMARC records are published for the client domain (hosting task), **when** the native "Send test email" action is used, **then** the test e-mail is delivered and passes the receiving server's SPF and DKIM checks, recorded in the go-live checklist.
**Given** an e-mail account password or client secret is entered, **when** configuration is exported (PLT-005), **then** the password and client secret are not exported (BR-PLT-013).

**Given** languages are added and published for a store (Language.Published, LimitedToStores), **when** a shopper opens the storefront, **then** the language selector lists only that store's published languages, and choosing one shows all interface text from that language's resources.

**Given** Kiswahili, English, French, Arabic, Russian and Mandarin are configured with translated resources (client content), **when** a shopper selects each in turn, **then** the interface text is shown in the selected language; untranslated resources show the default-language text and are reported by PLT-025.
**Given** English and Chichewa language packs are installed (interface text packs imported as resource XML), **when** a shopper selects Chichewa, **then** interface text appears in Chichewa.

**Given** Arabic is configured with Language.Rtl = true, **when** a shopper selects Arabic, **then** the storefront uses the right-to-left stylesheet (DefaultClean styles.rtl.css) and the admin follows LocalizationSettings.IgnoreRtlPropertyForAdminArea.

**Given** the country list is maintained, **when** a region or district list is imported for a country (CountryController.ImportCsv) as StateProvince records, **then** address forms offer those regions or districts for that country.

**Given** several currencies are published for a store with rates, **when** a shopper selects a currency, **then** prices and totals are shown in it, formatted by Currency.DisplayLocale or CustomFormatting and rounded by Currency.RoundingType.

**Given** the primary store currency and the primary exchange-rate currency are set (CurrencySettings.PrimaryStoreCurrencyId, PrimaryExchangeRateCurrencyId), **when** an order is placed in another currency, **then** order amounts are stored in the primary store currency with the customer currency and Order.CurrencyRate.

**Given** USD is set as the primary store currency, **when** the instance is configured, **then** all reports and order totals use USD as base; the settlement currency of each payment method is held by C-FX (PAY-023).
**Given** rates are maintained by hand, **when** an administrator edits Currency.Rate, **then** the new rate applies to prices shown after the save; automatic rates come from PLT-024.

**Given** DateTimeSettings.DefaultStoreTimeZoneId is set for the client, **when** an order is placed, **then** it is stored in UTC and shown in admin and storefront in the store time zone (or the customer's time zone if AllowCustomersToSetTimeZone is on).
**Given** a language with LanguageCulture is selected, **when** dates and numbers are shown, **then** they follow that culture's format.

**Given** the fiscal-year start month and day are set (new setting FiscalCalendarSettings, client layer), **when** a report requests fiscal periods through the PLT fiscal-calendar service, **then** periods start on the configured date in the store time zone and each order date falls in exactly one period.
**Given** the fiscal-year start is changed, **when** reports are rerun, **then** past figures are regrouped by the new periods, and the change is in the configuration history (PLT-004).

**Given** two stores exist in one client installation (a retail store and a trade store) with their own Url and Hosts, **when** a product is mapped only to the trade store (StoreMapping), **then** it is listed, searchable and purchasable only in the trade store.
**Given** a retail store is configured for consumers, **when** a guest or registered consumer browses it, **then** they see retail products and retail prices of that store.

**Given** a trade store is configured for business buyers (B2B pack: customer roles, tier prices per store, payment terms), **when** a bulk or international buyer signs in, **then** they see the trade catalogue and the prices for their role in that store (TierPrice.StoreId).
basis: Inference from REQ-KTDA-CUS-002 (B2B buyers, PH-INF); FIT (TierPrice.StoreId)

criterion: **Given** retail, bulk, contract-packaging and forward-contract offers are set up as separate products, stores or transaction types, **when** a buyer uses each, **then** each model is reachable in the store it is mapped to; the model-specific behaviour is delivered by CAT and ORD features.
basis: Inference from REQ-KTDA-PRJ-002 (business models; confirm with client)

criterion: **Given** a store-specific value is saved for a setting (for example the theme, a payment method store limit or a shipping rule), **when** each store is used, **then** each store applies its own value and other stores use the shared value (BR-PLT-011).

**Given** the PLT health endpoint is enabled (new plugin route; access by token or IP allow-list), **when** the monitoring platform calls it, **then** it returns the status of the database connection, the cache, the scheduled-task runner (last success time of each enabled task), the queued-e-mail backlog and the product release version, with no personal data; the native keepalive/index route remains for liveness.
**Given** request telemetry is exported to the monitoring platform, **when** the dashboard is opened, **then** it shows page views, API calls, error rates and response-time percentiles per instance.

**Given** key transactions are tagged (search, checkout, payment confirmation), **when** the performance dashboard is opened, **then** it shows the latency of each key transaction per instance over a chosen period.

**Given** an alert rule with a threshold is configured for a metric, **when** the metric crosses the threshold, **then** the monitoring platform raises an alert to the configured recipients; thresholds are client settings, default not stated.

**Given** several client instances report to the monitoring platform, **when** an operator opens the cross-client view, **then** health and usage of all instances are shown; client staff cannot open this view, and no instance stores another client's data (BR-PLT-003).

**Given** an instance runs on more than one web node, **when** it is configured, **then** DistributedCacheConfig.Enabled is true (Redis or SQL Server), media are on shared storage, data-protection keys are shared and every node has identical plugin folders (L1 section 6.4).

**Given** a new product module is delivered, **when** it is deployed, **then** it is a plugin added to the plugin folder and installed; no core file changes outside the L1 section 6.3 register (BR-PLT-041).

**Given** a release is deployed on AWS or Azure virtual machines or app services, **when** the smoke tests run, **then** they pass with no dependency on one cloud provider (the optional media plugins Misc.AzureBlob and Misc.CloudflareImages are not required; both are in InstallationConfig.DisabledPlugins by default).

**Given** the database runs on a separate server from the application servers, **when** users connect through a browser, **then** the instance works with the database, application and client tiers separated.

**Given** an instance is installed with the PostgreSQL or MySQL data provider (MySQL 8.0 or newer: 5.00.1 ships only the MySQL 8 type map and targets MySqlVersion.MySql80), **when** all product features are tested, **then** they work on that provider: every product plugin uses FluentMigrator 8.0.1 migrations and the nopCommerce data layer, with no provider-specific SQL (BR-PLT-040).
basis: REQ-MPC-ARC-003; FIT (MySqlDataProvider.cs:356; Libraries/Nop.Data/DataProviders/Fluentmigrator/NopMySql8TypeMap.cs, NopMySql5TypeMap removed; PostgreSqlDataProvider; Libraries/Nop.Data/Nop.Data.csproj:15-18)

criterion: **Given** Windows Server 2019 or newer with the .NET 10 runtime required by nopCommerce 5.00, **when** the release is deployed, **then** the smoke tests pass on that server.

**Given** scheduled database and file backups are configured at the database or hosting layer, **when** a backup runs during trading hours, **then** the storefront and admin keep working and the backup completes without locking out users.

**Given** the instance uses MySQL or PostgreSQL, **when** an administrator uses Maintenance > Backup database, **then** the native action is not offered for those providers (they throw "does not support backup"); backups are provided only by the external backup service.
basis: FIT (MySqlDataProvider and PostgreSqlDataProvider.BackupDatabaseAsync throw; MsSqlDataProvider implements it)

criterion: **Given** a recovery site or zone is set up, **when** a failover test is run, **then** the instance is restored on the recovery site from the latest backup and passes the smoke tests; the measured recovery time and data loss are recorded.

**Given** backups and restore tests run, **when** the backup report is produced, **then** it lists each backup (time, size, success or failure) and the date and result of the last restore test, and failures raise an alert.

**Given** the client theme, **when** storefront pages are opened at phone, tablet and desktop widths, **then** at each viewport width of the test plan (Proposed: 360, 768 and 1280 CSS pixels) no horizontal scroll bar appears (document width not greater than viewport width) and every menu entry, button and form field present at desktop width can be reached and used.
**Given** a phone browser (current Android and iOS default browsers), **when** a shopper browses, searches, adds to cart and checks out, **then** each step completes in the mobile browser.
**Given** a 360 px wide viewport, **when** each storefront page is opened, **then** content and controls fit the width.

**Given** a new or changed storefront or admin screen in an Increment, **when** it is checked with an automated WCAG 2.1 AA tool and a manual keyboard and screen-reader check, **then** no level A or AA failure remains open at the end of the Increment (Definition of Done 9).

**Given** admin views need fixes, **when** they are changed, **then** each change is a registered core modification (L1 section 6.3, PRD-PLT-018) committed separately and tagged with the PRD ID (BR-PLT-041).

**Given** the accessibility toggle is shown on the storefront, **when** a shopper switches on high contrast (Plt.Accessibility.HighContrast) or larger text (Plt.Accessibility.LargerText), **then** all pages use the high-contrast or larger-text style until switched off; the choice is kept for the customer (GenericAttribute) or the browser session for guests.
**Given** help tips are configured for a screen (route key) and role, **when** a user opens that screen, **then** the tips are shown in the user's language; screens without tips show none.

**Given** a guided tour is configured for a role (buyer, seller or staff), **when** a user of that role signs in for the first time, **then** the tour starts once; the user can skip it and replay it later (Plt.Help.TourReplay); completion is stored per user.

**Given** a user with Platform.Core.Help.CreateEditDelete, **when** creates or edits help tips, tour steps and links to training materials (documents in DOC-002 or content pages in MKT-007), per language, **then** the change is shown to users without a deployment.

**Given** the admin first-run steps exist natively (resources Admin.ConfigurationSteps.*) and AdminAreaSettings.ShowDocumentationReferenceLinks, **when** an administrator uses the admin area, **then** the native steps and links remain available alongside PLT tips.

**Given** retention rules exist for record types orders, payments, support tickets and logs (record type, period, action Archive, Anonymise or Delete, active flag; country then client layer), **when** the retention task runs, **then** records older than the period are processed by the action in batches; counts per type and action are written to the retention run log (AUD-PLT-009).

**Given** the action is Delete, **when** records are processed, **then** they are physically removed through the repository predicate delete, because the per-entity delete only sets Deleted for soft-deletable entities such as Order, Customer and Product (BR-PLT-050).
basis: FIT (EntityRepository.DeleteAsync: ISoftDeletedEntity sets Deleted; DeleteAsync(predicate) bulk-deletes)

criterion: **Given** the action is Archive, **when** records are processed, **then** they are written to the archive store with a manifest and checksum, verified, and only then removed from the live database.

**Given** a record is under legal hold (DOC-002) or is linked to an open payment, refund, dispute or receivable, **when** the retention task reaches it, **then** it is skipped and counted as held (BR-PLT-050).

**Given** native maintenance tasks exist (ClearLogTask, DeleteGuestsTask, DeleteInactiveCustomersTask), **when** a retention rule for logs or inactive customers is saved, **then** the matching native settings are set from the rule (CommonSettings.ClearLogOlderThanDays, GdprSettings.DeleteInactiveCustomersAfterMonths) so there is one source of the value.
**Given** a retention rule for tracking events (TRK-002) is configured, **when** the retention task runs, **then** tracking events older than the period are archived or deleted per the rule.
**Given** a retention rule is created or changed, **when** it is saved, **then** the change is recorded with old and new values (AUD-PLT-009) and, if the key is controlled, follows PLT-004.

**Given** product modules register their record types with the retention engine (IC-PLT-08: record type code, owning module, entity, date field that starts the period, allowed actions, hold check), **when** the retention rules screen is opened, **then** a rule can be set for each registered type, and the release registers at least: orders, payments, support tickets and logs (REQ-MPC-FR-322); DOC-002 document types by retention class; CRM tickets, call logs, inbound messages and ratings; IAM AuthEvent, UserSession, PolicyAcceptance, PrivacyRequest, VerificationCase and OtpChallenge; RET return data, dispute cases, case messages and evidence Downloads; TRK tracking events (active period, then archive period) and the notification log; the SEC-004 audit trail; AI-003 chat transcripts; the ADM-003 rule evaluation log and ADM-007 work drafts; every period is Not stated in source (BR-PLT-051).

**Given** a registered record type supplies a hold check (for example a DOC-002 legal hold, an open RET case or dispute, a record with a RET legal-hold flag), **when** the retention task reaches a record for which the check returns held, **then** the record is skipped and counted as held; it is never purged while held (BR-PLT-050).

**Given** the record type is the SEC-004 audit trail, **when** the retention task runs, **then** only whole closed audit segments past the period are processed, by archive (verified copy) or removal with the signed checkpoint that SEC-004 writes (BR-SEC-016); single audit events are never deleted or anonymised.

**Given** a retention rule for tracking events sets an active period and an archive period, **when** the retention task runs, **then** events past the active period move to the archive and stay searchable by staff; events past the archive period are deleted; notification-log entries follow their own rule; each run is logged (AUD-PLT-009).

**Given** a product release is built (nopCommerce tag plus product plugins, each with a version), **when** it is deployed to a client, **then** it is deployed to the test instance first, the regression set passes there, and only then is it deployed to the live instance (BR-PLT-060).

**Given** the new release starts, **when** the application starts, **then** native upgrade migrations (Libraries/Nop.Data/Migrations/UpgradeTo*) and plugin updates (IPluginService.UpdatePluginsAsync at AppStarted) run, and the instance records the release version.
basis: FIT (Libraries/Nop.Data/Migrations/UpgradeTo500: SchemaMigration, DataMigration, PriceListMigration, SearchTermMigration; Presentation/Nop.Web.Framework/Migrations/UpgradeTo500: SettingMigration, LocalizationMigration; AppStartedConsumer UpdatePluginsAsync)

criterion: **Given** the release has started, **when** the post-upgrade check runs, **then** it reports incompatible plugins (IPluginsInfo.IncompatiblePlugins, from plugin.json SupportedVersions), re-validates the applied pack set against the new key catalogue (PLT-003), and checks the extension register (ADM-001); each failure appears as a system warning (SystemWarningCreatedEvent) and in the upgrade run report.

**Given** any check fails on the live instance, **when** the platform team decides to roll back, **then** the pre-upgrade database backup and the previous application and plugin folders are restored; the upgrade run is marked RolledBack (SM-PLT-05).

**Given** the release contains registered core modifications (L1 section 6.3), **when** a new nopCommerce release is adopted, **then** the product fork is rebased on the new tag, each core commit tagged with its PRD ID is re-applied and the register-driven regression set is run (L1 section 6.2 principle 2).

**Given** an instance is upgraded from nopCommerce 4.90 to the 5.00 product release, **when** the native 5.00 setting migration runs, **then** the values of ordersettings.returnrequest* and numberofdaysreturnrequestavailable are copied to returnrequestsettings.*, the removed phone-validation keys are deleted, and the applied pack set is then re-validated (PLT-003); keys still named the 4.90 way in a client pack are reported as pack errors (Plt.PackKeyUnknown).

**Given** a product plugin or a third-party plugin (NopStation, Nop-Templates, FoxNetSoft, AFR extensions) is in the release, **when** the release is built and started, **then** the plugin targets net10.0, declares SupportedVersions "5.00" in plugin.json, references FluentMigrator 8.0.1 and calls only the asynchronous data, settings, localization, logging, event and store APIs; a plugin without a 5.00 build is reported in IPluginsInfo.IncompatiblePlugins and is not loaded, and the release is not deployed to a live instance (BR-PLT-097).

**Given** the release ships the feature definitions (PRD ID, name, pack, tier, phase, depends on, implementing plugins), **when** a user with Platform.Core.Features.View opens the registry, **then** every product feature is listed with its state for the client and for each store.

**Given** a feature is switched on or off, **when** it is saved, **then** the state is stored as setting productfeature.<prd-id> (StoreId 0 for the client, StoreId n for a store) and resolves store value, else client value, else off (BR-PLT-030); audited (AUD-PLT-007).
**Given** a feature depends on another feature that is off, **when** it is switched on, **then** the change is refused with message Plt.FeatureDependencyOff naming the dependency.
**Given** a feature of the Platform core tier, **when** it is switched off, **then** the change is refused with message Plt.FeatureAlwaysOn (decision D-01: Platform core is always on).

**Given** a feature is implemented by a plugin that is not installed, **when** it is switched on, **then** the plugin is queued for installation and the registry shows message Plt.RestartRequired; for plugin types that support store limits, store-level states are also written to the plugin's LimitedToStores (BR-PLT-012).

**Given** a product plugin calls the registry (IC-PLT-02) for feature F and store S, **when** F is off for S, **then** the feature's pages, widgets and actions are not shown for S and its scheduled work skips S.

**Given** source files in the migration format are uploaded, **when** a dry run is started, **then** every row is validated (required fields, references, duplicates) and a report lists rejected rows with reasons (Plt.MigrationRowInvalid); nothing is written.

**Given** the dry run has no blocking errors, **when** the import runs, **then** customers and orders are imported through the native importers (IImportManager.ImportCustomersFromXlsxAsync, ImportOrdersFromXlsxAsync); addresses through ICustomerService.InsertCustomerAddressAsync; loyalty balances as one opening entry per customer through IRewardPointService.AddRewardPointsHistoryEntryAsync; gift-card balances through IGiftCardService.InsertGiftCardAsync.

**Given** customer passwords are migrated as hashes, **when** the import runs, **then** hashed passwords are imported only if SecuritySettings.AllowStoreOwnerExportImportCustomersWithHashedPassword is on and the hash format matches; otherwise customers must reset their password.
**Given** an import is run again with the same source keys, **when** rows already imported are found in the source-to-target key map, **then** they are updated or skipped, not duplicated.

**Given** an import completes, **when** the reconciliation report runs, **then** for each entity type it shows source count, imported count, rejected count, and for money values (order totals, loyalty points, gift-card balances) source total and imported total; any difference is highlighted.

**Given** the new client also has customer or customer-group contract prices to migrate, **when** the import runs, **then** they are loaded as native price lists through the price-list Excel import (Catalog > Price lists > Import, IImportManager.ImportPriceListsFromXlsxAsync, permission Catalog.PriceListsImportExport) and counted in the reconciliation report like the other entities; the import stops on the first unknown product (native behaviour), so the dry run checks product references first.

**Given** a PLT rate-provider plugin implementing IExchangeRateProvider is installed and selected (CurrencySettings.ActiveExchangeRateProviderSystemName) with CurrencySettings.AutoUpdateEnabled on, **when** the native UpdateExchangeRateTask runs, **then** the provider returns rates relative to the primary exchange-rate currency and the task updates Currency.Rate for each matching currency.
**Given** the source is unavailable or returns an error, **when** the task runs, **then** no rate is changed and the error is written to the system log.

**Given** a returned rate differs from the current rate by more than the configured tolerance (setting, default not stated), **when** the provider prepares its result, **then** that rate is left out of the result, so it is not applied, and the deviation is logged for finance staff.

**Given** a target language exists, **when** content staff export for translation, **then** one file per language holds every locale resource (native ExportXml) and every localized entity field (new export), each with its source text and current translation.
**Given** a translated file is imported, **when** the import runs, **then** resources and localized fields are updated and marked Unchecked (BR-PLT-090).
**Given** the languages required by KTDA are configured, **when** the coverage report is opened, **then** it shows per language the share of resources and content fields translated and checked.
**Given** a translation is Unchecked, **when** a reviewer marks it Checked, **then** the status becomes Checked with reviewer and date (AUD-PLT-011).
**Given** the source text of a Checked translation changes, **when** it is saved, **then** the translation becomes Unchecked.

**Given** the AI-001 approval step is on and a user with the AI approval permission approves an AiTranslationDraft, **when** AI-001 writes the text to LocalizedProperty, **then** AI-001 calls IC-PLT-09 SetStatus and the PLT-025 translation status of that field and language becomes Checked with the approver and date; with the AI approval step off, AI-filled text is saved as Unchecked; PLT-025 is the only owner of translation status (BR-PLT-090).

**Given** machine pre-translation is enabled (TranslationSettings.AllowPreTranslate, TranslationServiceId Google Translate or DeepL), **when** a product is pre-translated, **then** the generated texts are marked Unchecked; the API keys (TranslationSettings.GoogleApiKey, DeepLAuthKey) are secrets never exported in a pack (BR-PLT-013).

**Given** the hosting profile document is produced for a deployment type (single node or web farm), **when** it is reviewed, **then** it lists every component hosted (application, database, cache, search engine, data warehouse, API gateway), its resource needs, and states the Malawi Post figures (4 cores at 2.0 GHz, 8 GB RAM, 2 TB storage, cloud hosting for the first 6 months) with whether the planned components fit within them.

**Given** decision C-SIZE states whether the Malawi Post figures are a floor or a ceiling, **when** the profile is finalised, **then** the profile shows the sizing that follows the decision — held by C-SIZE.

**Given** a key table has a row-version column (registered core modification, L1 section 6.3), **when** two users open the same record and both save, **then** the first save succeeds; the second update matches no row because the version changed, and the user sees message Plt.ConcurrencyConflict with the current values; nothing of the second save is written (BR-PLT-081).
basis: D; FC-M03-032; FIT (no RowVersion or concurrency token in 5.00.1 Libraries)

criterion: **Given** a state-changing request carries an idempotency key header, **when** the same key is received again from the same customer on the same route within the key retention period, **then** the stored response of the first execution is returned and the action is not executed again (BR-PLT-080).

**Given** two requests with the same key arrive at the same time, **when** both are processed, **then** one executes under ILocker key 'plt-idem-{key}'; the other waits and returns the stored response.
**Given** the same key arrives with a different request body, **when** it is processed, **then** it is refused as a key reuse and nothing is executed.

**Given** a state-changing public API call (IC-INT-01: POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE) is received, **when** it carries no idempotency key header, **then** it is refused with HTTP 400 and message Plt.IdempotencyKeyRequired and nothing is executed; with a key it follows BR-PLT-080 (the middleware covers every INT API route).

**Given** ReturnRequestSettings.ReturnRequestsEnabled is on, ReturnRequestSettings.ReturnRequestsForCompletedOrdersOnly is on and the order status is Complete, and fewer than ReturnRequestSettings.NumberOfDaysReturnRequestAvailable days have passed since the order was placed (0 = no limit), **when** the shopper opens the order details, **then** the return link is shown, and the return form lists only items whose product is not marked NotReturnable, is not a downloadable product (ReturnRequestSettings.DownloadableProductsReturnRequestsAllowed off) and whose quantity is not already requested in a return request that is not Cancelled.

**Given** the order is not Complete (with ReturnRequestsForCompletedOrdersOnly on) or the window has passed, **when** the shopper calls the return page of that order, **then** no return form is shown and the native controller redirects to the home page; no return request is created.
**Given** RET-002 eligibility rules are active, **when** the return form is prepared, **then** the items listed are those allowed by BR-RET-010 (see RET-002 (REQ-MPC-FR-237)).

**Given** the shopper enters a quantity for one or more items, picks one reason and one action from the configured lists and submits, **when** the request is accepted, **then** one native ReturnRequest is created per item with status Pending (RET status Requested, SM-RET-01) and a quantity capped at the quantity still available for return, a custom number from ReturnRequestSettings.ReturnRequestNumberMask, and the native NewReturnRequest.StoreOwnerNotification and NewReturnRequest.CustomerNotification messages are sent; RET also stores the reason ID and action ID, because the native record keeps only the localised names (BR-RET-002).
basis: FIT (5.00.1: ReturnRequestController.ReturnRequestSubmit, Presentation/Nop.Web/Controllers/ReturnRequestController.cs:209-318: quantity capped at line 267, custom number at 292); REQ-MPC-FR-227; REQ-KTDA-RET-001

criterion: **Given** ReturnRequestSettings.ReturnRequestsAllowFiles is on, **when** the shopper uploads a file larger than ReturnRequestSettings.ReturnRequestsFileMaximumSize (kilobytes), **then** the upload is refused with the native message ShoppingCart.MaximumUploadedFileSize and nothing is stored.

**Given** the RET evidence upload is enabled, **when** the shopper adds free-text details and several photos before submitting, **then** each file is stored as a native Download and linked to every return request of the submission (ReturnEvidence); the number of files is limited by a RET setting (default not stated) and above the limit message Ret.EvidenceLimit is shown; file type, size and scanning are applied by the ADM-008 upload policy for the upload context "return evidence" that RET registers with ADM-008, so a refused file gets Adm.UploadTypeNotAllowed or Adm.UploadTooLarge and is not stored; RET keeps no file-type check of its own (BR-RET-092).
basis: D (photos); REQ-MPC-FR-227; FIT (native keeps one file per request: ReturnRequest.UploadedFileId); SINGLE-FILTER

criterion: **Given** an evidence file of a return or case exists (native Download referenced by ReturnEvidence or by ReturnRequest.UploadedFileId), **when** anyone requests it through Nop.Web DownloadController.GetFileUpload or Admin DownloadController.DownloadFile with its GUID, **then** the single SEC-002 ownership filter (BR-SEC-005) asks the RET rule provider, which allows the shopper of the order, users of the vendor that owns the returned item, and staff holding Orders.ReturnRequestsView or Returns.Core.Cases.View; anyone else is refused by the SEC-002 filter and nothing is served (BR-RET-092).
basis: SINGLE-FILTER; Proposed; FIT (GetFileUpload(Guid downloadId) and Admin DownloadFile(Guid downloadGuid) serve any Download by GUID without an ownership check)

criterion: **Given** the shopper has return requests, **when** they open My account, Return requests (native CustomerReturnRequests page), **then** each request shows its number, item, quantity, reason, requested action, native status and date, and the RET detail: approval, return shipment and tracking reference, inspection outcome and refund state reported by PAY-016.

**Given** the client has published the returns-policy topic and set its system name in the RET settings, **when** the shopper opens the return form, **then** the policy text is shown on the form with a link to the full topic; the same topic system name is used by CAT-031 on product and order pages.

**Given** the administrator maintains the native return reasons and return actions, **when** they are saved, **then** they appear on the return form in their display order and in the shopper's language.

**Given** the administrator changes ReturnRequestSettings.NumberOfDaysReturnRequestAvailable (setting key returnrequestsettings.numberofdaysreturnrequestavailable) for a store, **when** an order of that store is checked, **then** the store value applies, otherwise the shared value (StoreId 0).

**Given** the product configuration pack is applied to a store, **when** the return settings are read, **then** ReturnRequestSettings.ReturnRequestsForCompletedOrdersOnly, ReturnReasonsEnabled and ReturnActionsEnabled are on, and GuestReturnRequestsAllowed, UseEuWithdrawalLocales and DownloadableProductsReturnRequestsAllowed are off (the 5.00.1 defaults); with ReturnReasonsEnabled or ReturnActionsEnabled off the native submit would store "not available" instead of the chosen reason or action, which BR-RET-002 relies on.

**Given** a rule marks category C not returnable, **when** a shopper opens the return form for an order with a product in C, **then** that item is not listed; other eligible items are listed (BR-RET-010).

**Given** a seller policy gives vendor V a return window of W days counted from the configured start (order date or delivery date), **when** W days have passed for an order line of V, **then** that line is not listed while lines of other sellers inside their window remain listed.

**Given** a product is marked NotReturnable (native) and a category rule says returnable, **when** eligibility is evaluated, **then** the product is not returnable: the native flag always wins, then product rule, then seller rule, then category rule, then the global setting (BR-RET-011).

**Given** RET-002 rules set any window, **when** the rules are saved, **then** RET checks that ReturnRequestSettings.NumberOfDaysReturnRequestAvailable is 0 or not shorter than the longest rule window, because the native order-level check runs first; otherwise the save is refused with message Ret.WindowSettingConflict.
basis: FIT (5.00.1: IsReturnRequestAllowedAsync checks the global window before availability, Libraries/Nop.Services/Orders/OrderProcessingService.cs:3169-3182); Proposed

criterion: **Given** a rule has conditions text (for example about the state of the item), **when** the shopper selects that item, **then** the conditions are shown on the form and the shopper must tick a confirmation before submitting.

**Given** a submitted form contains a quantity for an item that is not eligible, or more than the quantity still available, **when** the POST reaches ReturnRequestController.ReturnRequestSubmit, **then** a RET action filter on that action re-checks every line against BR-RET-010, refuses the whole submission, shows the form again with message Ret.ItemNotEligible and creates no ReturnRequest; the IReturnRequestService.InsertReturnRequestAsync override refuses any ineligible insert as a second guard (BR-RET-012).
basis: REQ-MPC-FR-237; FIT (5.00.1: the native submit, Presentation/Nop.Web/Controllers/ReturnRequestController.cs:244-267, skips lines without available quantity and caps each posted quantity at the quantity returned by GetReturnRequestAvailabilityAsync — the RET override, so ineligible lines are already never inserted — but it does so silently and checks ModelState only after inserting (line 314), so a ModelReceivedEvent veto cannot be used and the filter is kept to refuse the whole submission with a message)

criterion: **Given** a rule is created, changed or deleted, **when** it is saved, **then** who, when, old and new values are audited (AUD-RET-002).

**Given** a return is Approved and its shipping model allows pickup, **when** the shopper chooses pickup and an offered time slot, **then** a pickup booking is requested through the carrier adapter of LOG-021 (IC-RET-03, served by LOG IC-LOG-01 BookReturn where the adapter declares the reverse-booking capability) for the shopper's address, a ReturnShipment is created (SM-RET-03, status Booked) and the booking time is shown to the shopper (message Ret.PickupBooked).

**Given** a return is Approved and its shipping model allows drop-off, **when** the shopper chooses drop-off, **then** the outlets that accept returns (StorePickupPoint outlets of LOG-003 with the flag accepts returns, read through LOG IC-LOG-06 GetOutlets with the returns filter) are listed, and message Ret.DropOffInstructions is shown with the return reference.

**Given** the shipping model of the return requires a label, **when** the booking is confirmed, **then** a return label is generated through LOG-007 and offered as a PDF download on the return page; when no label is required, the instructions of the model are shown instead.

**Given** a return becomes Approved, **when** RET processes the approval, **then** a ReturnShipment with type (pickup or drop-off), destination and tracking reference (from the carrier, otherwise generated by RET with a check digit) is created and shown to the shopper and to the seller; RET registers the tracking reference with TRK through IC-TRK-01 RegisterExternalReference (owning module RET, entity type ReturnShipment, entity id) so that TRK-002 matches incoming events to it; a reference already registered for another entity is refused and RET generates a new one.

**Given** a ReturnShipment exists, **when** tracking events for its reference arrive through TRK-002, **then** the ReturnShipment status follows SM-RET-03; when it is delivered at the destination the return request becomes Received (SM-RET-01).

**Given** shipping models are configured with their payer, **when** a return is approved, **then** the model selected for the return is recorded on it; customer-paid and shared models create a return-delivery fee through RET-006; merchant-paid models charge the seller: RET calls IC-SEL-05 AddSellerCharge (source module RET, source type ReturnShipping, return reference, amount) and SEL-017 deducts it in the next settlement; client-subsidised models charge no one in the shop (BR-RET-020).

**Given** Malawi Post Table 10 is received, **when** models and selection rules are loaded from it, **then** the model applied to each return follows the Table 10 rules — held by T-MISS (Table 10 not provided).

**Given** destination rules are configured (seller-fulfilled items go to the seller address; client stock goes to the warehouse or outlet that shipped it — Proposed), **when** a return shipment is created, **then** its destination follows the rule; if the shopper dropped the item at an outlet that is not the destination, an onward task is created through LOG-011 where the Postal and logistics pack is active.

**Given** a return request is Received, **when** staff record the inspection with location, condition grade from the configured list, photos, notes and accepted quantity, **then** a ReturnInspection is created and linked to the return; the RET status becomes Accepted, PartiallyAccepted or InspectionRejected (SM-RET-01); the action is audited (AUD-RET-003).
**Given** a return request is not yet Received, **when** staff try to record an inspection, **then** it is refused with message Ret.StatusChangeNotAllowed and nothing changes.

**Given** the outcome is Accepted or PartiallyAccepted and the restock option is chosen, **when** the inspection is saved, **then** ReturnRequest.ReturnedQuantity is increased by the restocked quantity and the stock movement is posted once through the INV adjustment service (IC-INV-01 PostMovement, reason Return, with lot or serial number where tracked); RET does not change stock directly.
**Given** the outcome is Accepted or PartiallyAccepted, **when** the inspection is saved, **then** RET-005 starts the refund for the accepted quantity (see RET-005 (REQ-MPC-FR-232)).

**Given** the outcome is Accepted or PartiallyAccepted, **when** the inspection is saved and committed, **then** RET publishes the module event Return.Completed (OrderId, ReturnRequestIds, Outcome, AcceptedQuantity, CompletedOnUtc) once per return through IEventPublisher; ORD maps it to the order stage Returned where that stage is configured; consumers only notify or enqueue (BR-RET-064).

**Given** the outcome is InspectionRejected, **when** the inspection is saved, **then** the native status becomes RequestRejected, the shopper is told the reason, and may open a dispute case (RET-007).

**Given** the client allows seller inspection (setting) and the destination of the return is the seller, **when** the seller records the inspection through the RET seller endpoint, **then** the endpoint checks that the product belongs to the seller's vendor and applies the same rules as story 01.

**Given** an inspection accepts quantity q of order line L, **when** the inspection is saved, **then** RET creates a RefundTrigger (source Return) and calls the PAY-016 refund request (IC-RET-02) with the order, line L, quantity q, the amount of BR-RET-040 and the reason; PAY creates its Refund record (Initiated) and RET sets the return to RefundRequested (SM-RET-01).

**Given** a return is RefundRequested, **when** PAY reports Refund.Completed for it, **then** RET sets the return to Refunded, sets the native status ItemsRefunded through IReturnRequestService.UpdateReturnRequestAsync and the shopper receives the native ReturnRequestStatusChanged.CustomerNotification (BR-RET-030).

**Given** a return is RefundRequested, **when** PAY reports the refund waiting for approval or Failed, **then** the return stays RefundRequested, the PAY state is shown on the return, and no second request is sent.

**Given** an order with PaymentStatus Paid or PartiallyRefunded is cancelled, **when** the native OrderStatusChangedEvent (new status Cancelled) is raised, **then** the RET consumer only enqueues a RefundTrigger (source Cancellation); the RET task then requests from PAY-016 a refund of the amount still refundable (PAY applies BR-PAY-081); the native CancelOrderAsync itself refunds nothing.
basis: REQ-MPC-FR-232; FIT (CancelOrderAsync does not void or refund; consumers swallow exceptions)

criterion: **Given** a cancelled order has PaymentStatus Pending, **when** the cancellation is processed, **then** no refund is requested.

**Given** SVC-005 records a service failure for a paid service order and raises the module event Service.Failed (order, line, reason), **when** RET receives it, **then** a RefundTrigger (source ServiceFailure) is enqueued and processed as for cancellations; the amount rule for service failures is Not stated in source — requires confirmation.

**Given** an order has several lines and only one line is returned, in part, **when** the refund is requested, **then** the request covers only that line and the accepted quantity; fees, commission and split amounts are adjusted by PAY (BR-PAY-051).

**Given** a RefundTrigger exists for a source type and source ID, **when** the same source fires again (duplicate event, retry or a second inspection save), **then** no second refund request is sent: the trigger idempotency key is unique (BR-RET-041).

**Given** a module raises a trigger through IC-RET-04 with a source type registered for that module in BR-RET-042 (BookingCancellation, ProviderNoShow, DepositRefund from SVC-003 and SVC-004; PolicyIssueFailed, PartnerFulfilmentFailed from FIN-003 and FIN-005; ApplicationRejected from EGV-002; PartialSupply from ORD-006), the order lines and the amount computed by that module, **when** RET receives it, **then** RET checks the source type is registered for the calling module and the amount does not exceed the line amounts still refundable, then sends one refund request to PAY-016 as in story 01; an unregistered source type, or a registered type raised by another module, is refused and logged.

**Given** ORD-006 raises PartialSupply through IC-RET-04 (ORD side IC-ORD-05) with the PartialSupplyProposal as source ID and, per order line, the unavailable quantity and the amount ORD computed, **when** RET receives it, **then** one RefundTrigger per line is created with key RET-PartialSupply-{ProposalId}-{OrderItemId} and one refund request for those lines is sent to PAY-016; a repeat of the same proposal sends nothing (BR-RET-041).

**Given** a trigger concerns an amount that is not on an order line (shipping, payment fee, or a checkout-attribute charge such as the FIN-003 transit-insurance premium) and the raising module passes it as an order-level part (component and amount), **when** RET receives it, **then** RET checks the part does not exceed the order-level amount still refundable (Order.OrderTotal minus Order.RefundedAmount minus the line amounts of the same request) and passes it to PAY-016 with the lines; a paid-order Cancellation trigger includes the order-level remainder in the same way.
basis: Proposed; FIT (checkout-attribute prices are added at order level from CheckoutAttributesXml in OrderTotalCalculationService, with no OrderItem; native PartiallyRefundAsync takes an order amount)

criterion: **Given** CHK-004 placed several sub-orders under one group payment (BR-PAY-014), a later sub-order could not be saved (CheckoutSession PlacementException) and staff choose to refund it, **when** CHK raises a trigger through IC-RET-04 with source type PlacementFailure, the CheckoutSession as source ID, the PaymentTransaction ID and the share of the unsaved sub-order computed by CHK (BR-CHK-007), **then** RET creates one RefundTrigger without order or order line, keyed RET-PlacementFailure-{CheckoutSessionId}-0, and requests the refund of that share against the payment transaction from PAY-016; a second trigger for the same CheckoutSession sends nothing.

**Given** a restocking fee rule exists (fixed amount or percentage of the line amount, by category, seller or reason, with an effective date), **when** an inspection accepts the item, **then** the fee is calculated with the rule version in force on the return date, recorded on the return and deducted from the amount requested from PAY-016 (BR-RET-050).

**Given** the shipping model of the return is customer-paid or shared, **when** the return shipment is booked, **then** a return-delivery fee is recorded on the return from the configured fee rule (see RET-003 (REQ-MPC-FR-228)).

**Given** the fees of a return are higher than the refund amount, **when** the refund amount is calculated, **then** the refund requested is zero, no negative amount is sent and staff are alerted on the return.
**Given** fee rules apply to items selected on the return form, **when** the form is shown, **then** the estimated fees per item are shown with message Ret.FeesNotice before the shopper submits.
**Given** fees were deducted, **when** the shopper opens the return, **then** the refund breakdown shows the item amount, each fee and the net refund.
**Given** a fee rule is created or changed, **when** it is saved, **then** who, when, old and new values are audited (AUD-RET-005).

**Given** an order has been delivered and the issue type chosen (missing item, damaged item, wrong item, or another configured type) allows a case without a return, **when** the shopper reports it from the order page (entry point owned by CRM-014) with a description and evidence, **then** a DisputeCase of type OrderIssue opens (SM-RET-02, Open) with the order and items filled in, a case number, and message Ret.CaseOpened is shown; no ReturnRequest is created.

**Given** LOG-013 records a delivery outcome Lost, Damaged or ReturnedToSender for a shipment of a paid order, **when** RET receives the LOG module event DeliveryOutcomeRecorded (OrderId, ShipmentId, Outcome; IC-LOG-05), **then** the consumer only enqueues; the RET task opens an OrderIssue case for the order (source LOG-013) unless one is open for that shipment, and the shopper receives message Ret.CaseOpened; any refund follows only from a remedy accepted in the case (RefundTrigger source Case).
**Given** an issue type is configured as not allowed without a return, **when** the shopper reports that issue, **then** the shopper is sent to the return form (RET-001) instead.

**Given** a case exists, **when** support staff open it, **then** the case view shows status, type, parties (customer, seller, client staff), linked order, return, ticket (CRM-006) and payment, the evidence list, and the event log with actor and time of each step and decision.

**Given** staff record a decision (outcome, reasons, remedy: refund, replacement, repair or none, and amount), **when** it is saved, **then** the decision is written to the case log (AUD-RET-007) and the case becomes RemedyProposed; message Ret.RemedyProposed is sent to the shopper.

**Given** a proof-of-delivery record exists for a shipment of the order (LOG-012), **when** a case is opened for that order, or the record arrives later (LOG module event ProofOfDeliveryRecorded, IC-LOG-05, consumed by enqueue only), **then** the record is linked to the case as evidence of type ProofOfDelivery.

**Given** a case is RemedyProposed, **when** the shopper accepts in My account, **then** the case becomes RemedyAccepted; a refund remedy is requested through RET-005 (RefundTrigger source Case); when the remedy is done the case becomes Closed.

**Given** a case is RemedyProposed, **when** the shopper rejects with a reason, **then** the case returns to UnderInvestigation, or becomes Escalated if the configured number of rejections is reached (default not stated).

**Given** a case is RemedyProposed and the shopper has not answered within the acceptance wait time (setting, default not stated), **when** the wait time expires, **then** the case is flagged for staff; staff may close it as ClosedNoResponse with a reason; it is never closed automatically.
**Given** a case moves to a new step, **when** the step starts, **then** a timer for that step starts in the SLA component (CRM-014) and its due time is shown on the case.

**Given** a case is not resolved at the internal levels, **when** staff escalate it to the client's dispute process, **then** the case becomes Escalated, is assigned to the next level of the escalation matrix and the escalation is audited (AUD-RET-008); the Malawi Post levels follow its Complaints and ADR Policy — held by T-MISS (policy not provided).

**Given** the client has published the dispute-process topic and set its system name in the RET settings, **when** a case is opened or viewed, **then** the case page links to the topic; the same topic is used by CAT-031 on product and order pages.

**Given** PAY-007, PAY-035 or PAY-036 calls OpenCase (IC-RET-01) for an order, **when** the call is processed, **then** a case of type PaymentDispute opens with the source module and reference; HasOpenCase(orderId) returns true until the case is Closed, ClosedNoResponse, Withdrawn or ClosedExternal (BR-RET-062).

**Given** a case of any type is open for an order, **when** ORD-002 checks HasOpenCase (IC-RET-01) before recording buyer or deemed acceptance, **then** true is returned and ORD refuses the acceptance; once every case of the order is in a closed state false is returned.

**Given** CAT-024 raises Listing.Withdrawn for a product, **when** the RET consumer receives it, **then** the consumer only enqueues; the RET task flags every open case of an order that contains the product in the cases queue with the withdrawal reference; no case status, remedy or refund changes (BR-CAT-015).

**Given** an SLA policy exists for a case type and category, with a metric (seller response or resolution) and a duration (values not stated), **when** a case of that type opens, **then** a timer starts in the SLA component (CRM-014); the due time is shown on the case and in the queue.

**Given** a timer passes its due time, **when** the SLA task runs, **then** the case is marked Breached, escalated one level in the matrix, and the assignee and the next level are notified; the breach is audited (AUD-RET-008).

**Given** the case is waiting for the customer and the policy pauses on that state (setting), **when** the case enters that state, **then** the resolution timer pauses and resumes when the customer answers.

**Given** a triage rule "reason code R and order value above V gives priority P and queue Q" is active (values configured), **when** a case with reason R and a higher order value opens, **then** the case gets priority P and queue Q, and the rule applied is written to the case log.

**Given** external escalation is allowed for the case category and the external bodies are configured, **when** a support manager escalates the case externally, **then** the case becomes EscalatedExternal, a case file is generated (summary PDF, evidence files and the case log including messages, in one ZIP), its hash is recorded and the export is audited (AUD-RET-008).
**Given** a case is EscalatedExternal, **when** staff record the external outcome, **then** the case becomes ClosedExternal with the outcome and reference recorded.

**Given** escalation-matrix levels are configured per category (internal steps and external points), **when** a case is escalated, **then** it moves to the next configured level; the Malawi Post levels follow its Complaints and ADR Policy — held by T-MISS (policy not provided).

**Given** return and dispute service-level standards and their escalation actions are configured, **when** a return or case misses a standard, **then** the configured escalation action runs (notify, raise priority, move up a level).

**Given** retention rules for the RET record types (return data, dispute cases, case messages, evidence files) are set in PLT-020 (periods not stated), **when** the retention period of a closed case or return has passed, **then** the PLT-020 job archives or deletes the records and their Download files as the rule says; records of open cases or with a legal-hold flag are never purged; each purge is audited (AUD-RET-010).

**Given** the user has Returns.Core.Reports.View, **when** they run the returns and disputes report for a period, **then** it shows return rate (items returned divided by items sold in the period, definition Proposed), returns and cases by reason code, resolution time from open to close, and outcomes, and can be exported to Excel.
**Given** a report period is configured (setting, default not stated), **when** the period ends, **then** a scheduled task generates the report for that period and stores it for download.

**Given** a return request is for an order item whose product belongs to vendor V, **when** a user of vendor V opens the RET seller return list, **then** the request is listed with order, item, quantity, reason, evidence and due time; requests of other vendors are not listed.
basis: REQ-MPC-FR-230; FIT (admin ReturnRequestController has no vendor filter)

criterion: **Given** a seller calls the detail of a return of another vendor, **when** the request is processed, **then** access is denied and nothing is shown (ownership check through OrderItem to Product.VendorId).

**Given** a return is Requested, **when** the seller approves, rejects with a reason, or asks the shopper for more information, **then** the response is recorded, the RET status changes per SM-RET-01, the shopper is notified and the response is audited (AUD-RET-011).

**Given** a return request is created for a product of vendor V, **when** it is saved, **then** the seller receives the RET event code Returns.Core.SellerReturnRequested through IC-TRK-04 SendEvent (TRK-005 channels; the native NewReturnRequest template goes only to the store owner).

**Given** the seller response time (RET-008 SLA policy) passes without a response, **when** the SLA task runs, **then** the configured action applies: escalate to client support staff, or approve automatically (setting; default not stated).
**Given** a seller rejected a return, **when** client support staff override with a reason, **then** the return moves to Approved and the override is audited (AUD-RET-011).

**Given** a case of type ReturnDispute or BuyerSellerDispute is linked to vendor V, **when** the shopper posts a message with optional attachments, **then** the message is stored with sender and time, shown to the seller of V and to client staff, and the seller is notified.

**Given** a case is linked to vendor V, **when** a user of V replies through the seller portal, **then** the reply is shown to the shopper and staff; users who are not parties or staff cannot read the thread (access denied).

**Given** a message breaks the moderation rules, **when** a user with Returns.Core.Cases.Moderate hides it with a reason, **then** the parties see message Ret.MessageHidden in its place, the original is kept in the case record, and the action is audited (AUD-RET-009).
**Given** pre-moderation is on for the store (setting, default not stated), **when** a party posts a message, **then** the message is held until staff release it.
**Given** staff join the case as mediator, **when** they record a decision with reasons, **then** the decision follows the RET-007 remedy flow (RemedyProposed, customer acceptance).

**Given** a case is exported (RET-008), **when** the case file is generated, **then** the full message thread, including hidden messages and moderation actions, is in the file (see RET-008 (REQ-MPC-FR-247)).

**Given** a user may access the admin area, **when** they open the admin home page, **then** the native dashboard shows common statistics, order and customer statistics charts, latest orders, popular search terms, bestsellers by quantity and by amount, incomplete orders and order averages, each card only if the user holds its native permission.

**Given** a product plugin needs a dashboard panel, **when** the plugin registers a widget for an admin dashboard widget zone (for example admin_dashboard_top), **then** the panel is shown on the dashboard without changing native views.

**Given** orders exist in the period, **when** the user runs Sales summary grouped by day, week or month with order and payment status filters, **then** sales totals per group are shown (actual sales).
basis: FIT (ReportController.SalesSummary; GroupByOptions Day, Week, Month); REQ-KTDA-ANL-002

criterion: **Given** orders exist in the period, **when** the user runs Bestsellers sorted by quantity or amount, **then** products are ranked, giving the fast movers.
